boundary_rationale: The unit opens with a regnal-year time-frame, וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת אַחַ֗ת לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס (“in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia” web:Ezra.1.1), immediately fused to a fulfillment clause, לִכְל֥וֹת דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה מִפִּ֣י יִרְמְיָ֑ה (“that Yahweh's word by Jeremiah's mouth might be accomplished” web:Ezra.1.1, oshb:Ezra.1.1). Narration then supplies a proclamation frame, וַיַּֽעֲבֶר קוֹל֙ בְּכָל מַלְכוּת֔וֹ וְגַם בְּמִכְתָּ֖ב לֵאמֹֽר (“he made a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and put it also in writing, saying” web:Ezra.1.1, oshb:Ezra.1.1), which hands directly into the king's own quoted words opening Ezra.1.2, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֗ר כֹּ֚רֶשׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס (“Cyrus king of Persia says” web:Ezra.1.2, oshb:Ezra.1.2). The quotation runs as one continuous edict carried by its own volitive chain, יְהִ֤י ... וְיַ֕עַל ... וְיִ֗בֶן (Ezra.1.3, oshb:Ezra.1.3), which the directive יְנַשְּׂא֨וּהוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י מְקֹמ֔וֹ (“let the men of his place help him” web:Ezra.1.4, oshb:Ezra.1.4) carries forward through the closing clause of Ezra.1.4, עִם הַ֨נְּדָבָ֔ה לְבֵ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם (“the free will offering for God's house which is in Jerusalem” web:Ezra.1.4, oshb:Ezra.1.4). That directive modality is cut off precisely at Ezra.1.5's wayyiqtol, וַיָּק֜וּמוּ (“Then ... rose up” web:Ezra.1.5, oshb:Ezra.1.5), under a wholly fresh subject (the returning heads of households) -- the edict's own volitive-chain opening and its termination by that wayyiqtol, not chapter or verse numbering or WEB's punctuation, set both edges.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Ezra.1.1 through Ezra.1.11 as one undivided decree-to-vessels row loses the edict's own volitive-chain closure at Ezra.1.4 and the subject pivot to the community's own response marked by Ezra.1.5's wayyiqtol וַיָּק֜וּמוּ.

boundary_rationale: Narration resumes with a wayyiqtol opener naming the responders, וַיָּק֜וּמוּ רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָב֗וֹת לִֽיהוּדָה֙ וּבִנְיָמִ֔ן וְהַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֑ם (“Then the heads of fathers' households of Judah and Benjamin, the priests and the Levites” web:Ezra.1.5, oshb:Ezra.1.5), whose subject the asyndetic relative clause לְכֹ֨ל הֵעִ֤יר הָאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת רוּח֔וֹ (“all whose spirit God had stirred” web:Ezra.1.5, oshb:Ezra.1.5) extends, echoing the king's own stirring in Ezra.1.1, הֵעִ֣יר יְהוָ֗ה אֶת ר֨וּחַ֙ (“Yahweh stirred up the spirit” web:Ezra.1.1, oshb:Ezra.1.1) -- the same stirring-of-spirit collocation binding king's response and people's response as one movement (purpose itself is carried separately, by the infinitive pair לַעֲל֣וֹת לִבְנ֔וֹת later in the verse). Ezra.1.6 continues that same donative movement under a widened subject, וְכָל סְבִיבֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ חִזְּק֣וּ בִֽידֵיהֶ֔ם (“All those who were around them strengthened their hands” web:Ezra.1.6, oshb:Ezra.1.6), 1:6 and Ezra.1.7's own opener, וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ כּ֔וֹרֶשׁ הוֹצִ֖יא (“Cyrus the king brought out” web:Ezra.1.7, oshb:Ezra.1.7), sharing that disjunctive waw-fronted-subject-qatal clause type -- but Ezra.1.5 itself opens with a wayyiqtol, וַיָּק֜וּמוּ, not that pattern, so clause form alone would put a seam at 1:5|1:6, not at 1:6|1:7, and cannot be the differentiator this row needs. What does differentiate them is content: Ezra.1.5-Ezra.1.6 share one donor-action class (gift-giving) with a widening beneficiary field, while Ezra.1.7 introduces a new agent (the king) and a new object class (temple vessels restored from the royal treasury, not a free-will gift) -- that actor/action-class break, not clause form, closes the unit before Ezra.1.7.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting Ezra.1.5 (the rising) from Ezra.1.6 (the neighbors' gifts) into two rows overstates a minor actor-shift within one continuous donor-action-class mobilization wave; clause form does not decide the question either way, since 1:5 opens with a wayyiqtol while 1:6 and Ezra.1.7's accepted seam alone share the disjunctive waw-subject-qatal pattern; the content-level break at Ezra.1.7 (new agent, new object class) is what actually closes the unit, not any clause-type contrast internal to 1:5-1:6.

boundary_rationale: A fresh subject opens the unit, וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ כּ֔וֹרֶשׁ הוֹצִ֖יא (“Also Cyrus the king brought out” web:Ezra.1.7, oshb:Ezra.1.7), naming the temple vessels Nebuchadnezzar had earlier removed; the action runs through a chain of narrative verbs ending וַֽיִּסְפְּרֵם֙ לְשֵׁשְׁבַּצַּ֔ר הַנָּשִׂ֖יא (“and counted them out to Sheshbazzar the prince” web:Ezra.1.8, oshb:Ezra.1.8). Ezra.1.9 opens its own list with a demonstrative-fronted presentative clause, וְאֵ֖לֶּה מִסְפָּרָ֑ם (“This is the number of them” web:Ezra.1.9, oshb:Ezra.1.9) -- a bare demonstrative subject over a suffixed-noun predicate, formally paralleling Ezra.2.1's own register opener -- switching from finite-verb transfer narration to bare itemized enumeration. That syntactic-class switch, not the demonstrative alone, is the operative warrant: the same demonstrative pronoun also does sub-unit-level work elsewhere in the book (it opens a sub-register within the larger chapter-2 list at Ezra.2.59, and at Ezra.8.13, וּמִבְּנֵ֣י אֲדֹנִיקָם֮ אַחֲרֹנִים֒, it is not even clause-initial), so the incipit by itself cannot carry this seam. The item lines run through Ezra.1.10, and the unit closes on a colophon totaling the class and naming the carrier, כָּל כֵּלִים֙ לַזָּהָ֣ב וְלַכֶּ֔סֶף חֲמֵ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְאַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֑וֹת הַכֹּ֞ל הֶעֱלָ֣ה שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּ֗ר (“All the vessels of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought all these up” web:Ezra.1.11, oshb:Ezra.1.11).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading Ezra.1.7 through Ezra.1.11 as one undivided transfer unit, hosting the inventory as an inset, is the stronger rival: Ezra.1.11's colophon closes עִ֚ם הֵעָל֣וֹת הַגּוֹלָ֔ה מִבָּבֶ֖ל לִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (“when the captives were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem” web:Ezra.1.11, oshb:Ezra.1.11), resuming the very participant and transaction narrated at Ezra.1.8's וַֽיִּסְפְּרֵם֙ לְשֵׁשְׁבַּצַּ֔ר, and the demonstrative opener at Ezra.1.9 is not exclusive to full-unit openings elsewhere in the book. This row holds the finer Ezra.1.7-Ezra.1.8 | Ezra.1.9-Ezra.1.11 cut on the syntactic-class switch from narrated-transfer finite verbs to headless numeral enumeration at Ezra.1.9, against the coarser inset reading's own resumption of 1:8's transaction at 1:11.

boundary_rationale: The list opens on its own incipit, a demonstrative-fronted presentative (verbless-clause) opener, וְאֵ֖לֶּה מִסְפָּרָ֑ם (“This is the number of them” web:Ezra.1.9, oshb:Ezra.1.9) -- a bare demonstrative subject over a suffixed-noun predicate, no construct chain -- formally paralleling Ezra.2.1's own register opener, וְאֵ֣לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י הַמְּדִינָ֗ה (“Now these are the children of the province” web:Ezra.2.1, oshb:Ezra.2.1), whose predicate בְּנֵ֣י הַמְּדִינָ֗ה is a genuine construct chain with the demonstrative standing outside it as subject: the shared device is the demonstrative-fronted presentative pattern, not a shared construct state. The item lines (platters, knives, bowls) run through Ezra.1.10, and the unit closes on a colophon totaling the class and naming the carrier, כָּל כֵּלִים֙ לַזָּהָ֣ב וְלַכֶּ֔סֶף חֲמֵ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְאַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֑וֹת הַכֹּ֞ל הֶעֱלָ֣ה שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּ֗ר (“All the vessels of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought all these up” web:Ezra.1.11, oshb:Ezra.1.11), closing with עִ֚ם הֵעָל֣וֹת הַגּוֹלָ֔ה מִבָּבֶ֖ל לִירוּשָׁלִָֽם (“when the captives were brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem” web:Ezra.1.11, oshb:Ezra.1.11) -- language sharing ordinary book-wide diction with Ezra.2.1's own captivity vocabulary (the golah lexeme recurs 12 times across 7 chapters, no seam-discriminating force on its own) and so hands forward to the golah register without merging into it, since the colophon still closes with its own total rather than opening a new one.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the colophon's captivity language at Ezra.1.11 as already opening the Ezra.2.1 register would erase the colophon's own close of the vessel unit and the topic change from precious metal to returning persons.

boundary_rationale: A new register opens on וְאֵ֣לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י הַמְּדִינָ֗ה (“Now these are the children of the province” web:Ezra.2.1, oshb:Ezra.2.1), specifying its members as הָֽעֹלִים֙ מִשְּׁבִ֣י הַגּוֹלָ֔ה (“who went up out of the captivity of those who had been carried away” web:Ezra.2.1, oshb:Ezra.2.1) -- picking up the הַגּוֹלָ֔ה vocabulary Ezra.1.11's colophon had just used for the vessel-carrying. Ezra.2.2 names the caravan's leaders through the verse's atnach on בַּעֲנָ֑ה, then pivots -- in the verse's second half -- to its own transition phrase, מִסְפַּ֕ר אַנְשֵׁ֖י עַ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (“The number of the men of the people of Israel” web:Ezra.2.2, oshb:Ezra.2.2), which syntactically heads the clan-by-clan enumeration beginning at Ezra.2.3 rather than closing the leader-roster frame that precedes the atnach; this row keeps it inside Ezra.2.1-Ezra.2.2 because whole-verse granularity governs this part's grain (no sub-verse rows), not because the heading itself belongs to the frame. The unit closes at the end of Ezra.2.2 because Ezra.2.3 is where a name-plus-figure line actually begins, בְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔שׁ אַלְפַּ֕יִם מֵאָ֖ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם (“The children of Parosh, two thousand one hundred seventy-two” web:Ezra.2.3, oshb:Ezra.2.3) -- nothing in Ezra.2.1-Ezra.2.2 itself is a counted entry. Ezra.1.11 closes the preceding vessel colophon immediately before this incipit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two closer rivals were weighed and set aside at whole-verse grain: ending the frame at Ezra.2.2's own atnach (on בַּעֲנָ֑ה), which would treat מִסְפַּ֕ר אַנְשֵׁ֖י עַ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵֽל as opening the following count rather than closing this row -- rejected because this part's grain does not split within a verse; and extending this row through Ezra.2.3 to give the incipit a worked counted example, which would blur the formal line between the register's own frame (name + transition phrase, no figures) and its entries (name + figure, repeated).

boundary_rationale: This is one uninterrupted run of name-plus-figure entries opening בְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔שׁ אַלְפַּ֕יִם מֵאָ֖ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם (“The children of Parosh, two thousand one hundred seventy-two” web:Ezra.2.3, oshb:Ezra.2.3) and closing בְּנֵ֣י סְנָאָ֔ה שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֔ים וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת וּשְׁלֹשִֽׁים (“The children of Senaah, three thousand six hundred thirty” web:Ezra.2.35, oshb:Ezra.2.35). No entry in this stretch carries a determined-state class caption of its own; the variation that does occur is formulaic: the construct-chain form בְּנֵ֣י ('sons/children of') spans the whole run (Ezra.2.3-Ezra.2.21, Ezra.2.24-Ezra.2.26, Ezra.2.29-Ezra.2.35), while the alternate, place-linked form אַנְשֵׁ֥י ('men of') is confined to two interleaved pairs, Ezra.2.22-Ezra.2.23 and Ezra.2.27-Ezra.2.28, never attested before Ezra.2.22 (sweep.py --web 'The men of' returns 7 hits book-wide; sweep.py --skel confirms 10 Hebrew-skeleton hits, only 4 of which fall inside Ezra.2.3-Ezra.2.35). Interleaving after Ezra.2.23, not symmetric recurrence around it, is what shows the alternation tracks no content boundary. The row closes because Ezra.2.36 opens with an absolute-state caption standing outside the count formula, הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים (“The priests” web:Ezra.2.36, oshb:Ezra.2.36), a different grammatical class of opener from anything inside this row.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this run at any of the sons-of/men-of alternations (Ezra.2.21|Ezra.2.22, Ezra.2.23|Ezra.2.24, Ezra.2.26|Ezra.2.27) would treat ordinary lexical variation -- not a class boundary -- as equivalent to Ezra.2.36's genuine caption break, which it is not.

boundary_rationale: An absolute-state caption opens the unit, הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים בְּנֵ֤י יְדַֽעְיָה֙ לְבֵ֣ית יֵשׁ֔וּעַ (“The priests: the children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua” web:Ezra.2.36, oshb:Ezra.2.36), a class header standing grammatically apart from the construct-chain entries of the laity roll it follows. Three more priestly clans are counted, closing בְּנֵ֣י חָרִ֔ם אֶ֖לֶף וְשִׁבְעָ֥ה עָשָֽׂר (“The children of Harim, one thousand seventeen” web:Ezra.2.39, oshb:Ezra.2.39). The row ends there because Ezra.2.40 opens a parallel absolute-state caption for a different personnel class, הַלְוִיִּ֑ם (“The Levites” web:Ezra.2.40, oshb:Ezra.2.40) -- the same captioning device marking a fresh boundary rather than continuing the priestly count.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying the priestly roll forward into Ezra.2.40 through Ezra.2.42 as one 'cultic personnel' row would erase two independent class captions (Ezra.2.36's and Ezra.2.40's) that the text itself supplies.

boundary_rationale: Three short cultic-support rolls share this unit, but they are not uniform in shape. Ezra.2.40 and Ezra.2.41 each open a bare absolute-state class caption, standing alone before its entry: הַלְוִיִּ֑ם (“The Levites” web:Ezra.2.40, oshb:Ezra.2.40) and הַֽמְשֹׁרְרִ֑ים (“The singers” web:Ezra.2.41, oshb:Ezra.2.41), each followed by one named sub-family and its own total (seventy-four; one hundred twenty-eight). Ezra.2.42's opener, בְּנֵ֣י הַשֹּֽׁעֲרִ֗ים (“The children of the gatekeepers” web:Ezra.2.42, oshb:Ezra.2.42), is a construct chain -- the shape of an ordinary entry line, formally identical to בְּנֵ֣י חָרִ֔ם at Ezra.2.39 -- not a third bare caption; the verse goes on to name six sub-families and closes on its own colophon total, הַכֹּ֕ל מֵאָ֖ה שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְתִשְׁעָֽה (“in all one hundred thirty-nine” web:Ezra.2.42, oshb:Ezra.2.42) -- the same הַכֹּ֕ל totaling device that closes the vessel inventory at Ezra.1.11 and recurs seven times book-wide (sweep, skeleton tier: 2 in these two lists -- Ezra.1.11, Ezra.2.42 -- and 5 more in the chapter 8 treasure register -- Ezra.8.25, Ezra.8.28, Ezra.8.30, Ezra.8.33, Ezra.8.35). All three classes are nonetheless minor cultic-support personnel, each far smaller in scale and textual weight than the priestly roll immediately before them (Ezra.2.36-Ezra.2.39; its opening entry, Ezra.2.36, already counts nine hundred seventy-three), and none opens a stretch long enough to carry its own multi-verse row at this part's grain; that shared minor scale, not a shared caption shape, is what keeps Levites, singers, and gatekeepers in one row. The row closes because Ezra.2.43 opens a caption for an unrelated, non-cultic personnel class, הַנְּתִינִ֑ים (“The temple servants” web:Ezra.2.43, oshb:Ezra.2.43), beginning the next, longer bloc.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting Levites (Ezra.2.40), singers (Ezra.2.41), and gatekeepers (Ezra.2.42) into three separate rows is defensible on caption grounds -- each does open its own class name, and Ezra.2.42 in particular is a compact sub-register with six internal entries and its own colophon, not a bare one-line caption matching Ezra.2.40-Ezra.2.41's shape -- and it would bring this stretch into line with the caption-driven boundaries this part uses elsewhere (Ezra.2.36's and Ezra.2.40's own captions each open a fresh row). This row instead groups the three on minor shared scale relative to the priesthood, a real but coarser-grained call than the caption rule alone would produce.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens הַנְּתִינִ֑ים (“The temple servants” web:Ezra.2.43, oshb:Ezra.2.43) and runs a name list through Ezra.2.54; a second caption at Ezra.2.55, בְּנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה (“The children of Solomon's servants” web:Ezra.2.55, oshb:Ezra.2.55), opens a further name list through Ezra.2.57. Both lists are gathered into a single joint colophon, כָּ֨ל הַנְּתִינִ֔ים וּבְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה (“All the temple servants, and the children of Solomon's servants, were three hundred ninety-two” web:Ezra.2.58, oshb:Ezra.2.58); neither sub-list is totaled on its own, so the colophon itself argues against splitting them. Ezra.2.42 closes the preceding cultic-personnel bloc right before this unit's opening caption. The row ends there because Ezra.2.59 opens a fresh incipit, וְאֵ֗לֶּה הָֽעֹלִים֙ (“These were those who went up” web:Ezra.2.59, oshb:Ezra.2.59), for a differently defined group.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the nethinim (Ezra.2.43 through Ezra.2.54) from Solomon's servants (Ezra.2.55 through Ezra.2.57) at their separate captions ignores that Ezra.2.58's colophon totals both classes jointly without supplying either sub-list with its own figure.

boundary_rationale: A fresh incipit opens the unit, וְאֵ֗לֶּה הָֽעֹלִים֙ (“These were those who went up” web:Ezra.2.59, oshb:Ezra.2.59), naming places rather than an articular (definite) class noun -- the shape carried instead by comparanda such as הַנְּתִינִ֑ים at Ezra.2.43 -- and states the group's problem: וְלֹ֣א יָֽכְל֗וּ לְהַגִּ֤יד בֵּית אֲבוֹתָם֙ וְזַרְעָ֔ם אִ֥ם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵֽם (“they could not show their fathers' houses and their offspring, whether they were of Israel” web:Ezra.2.59, oshb:Ezra.2.59). Ezra.2.61 continues the same problem among priests with a conjunctive, מִן-partitive opener, וּמִבְּנֵי֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים (“Of the children of the priests” web:Ezra.2.61, oshb:Ezra.2.61), a different shape from both the list-restart incipit at Ezra.2.59 and from the bare articular class-header captions active elsewhere in this chapter (הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים at Ezra.2.36, הַלְוִיִּ֑ם at Ezra.2.40, הַֽמְשֹׁרְרִ֑ים at Ezra.2.41, הַנְּתִינִ֑ים at Ezra.2.43); the vav-plus-מִן construction marks Ezra.2.61 as continuation of Ezra.2.59's unresolved-lineage problem, not a fresh caption of either type. Ezra.2.62 refers back to that same combined group with a demonstrative subject governing a finite qatal, אֵ֗לֶּה בִּקְשׁ֧וּ כְתָבָ֛ם הַמִּתְיַחְשִׂ֖ים (“These sought their place among those who were registered by genealogy” web:Ezra.2.62, oshb:Ezra.2.62) -- bare אֵ֗לֶּה, unlike Ezra.2.59's vav-prefixed וְאֵ֗לֶּה, and an ordinary finite clause besides, not the vav-prefixed verbless-presentative pattern this book's registers most often use to reopen a list. Sweep, skeleton tier: 6 book-wide, one a false positive (Ezra.6.12 וֵֽאלָהָ֞א, 'and God', not the demonstrative); of the 5 genuine attestations, the 4 that stand verse-initial each open a unit -- וְאֵ֖לֶּה מִסְפָּרָ֑ם at Ezra.1.9, וְאֵ֣לֶּה at Ezra.2.1, וְאֵ֗לֶּה at Ezra.2.59, and וְאֵ֛לֶּה at Ezra.8.1 -- while the 5th, וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמוֹתָ֔ם at Ezra.8.13, sits verse-medial inside an already-running entry and opens nothing; the pattern is one of at least two attested unit-opening shapes in these register chapters, alongside the bare articular class-header captions already conceded above (Ezra.2.36, Ezra.2.40, Ezra.2.41, Ezra.2.43). Both the missing vav and the finite (rather than verbless) predicate keep Ezra.2.62 from reopening the list the way Ezra.2.59 itself does. Ezra.2.60's own total, שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם (“six hundred fifty-two” web:Ezra.2.60, oshb:Ezra.2.60), closes the unclaimed-laity figure within this same unresolved-status stretch rather than marking a sub-seam; unlike the withheld sub-totals that keep Ezra.2.43-Ezra.2.58 one unit, the status of both groups here -- laity and priests alike -- remains open until the governor's ruling, and it is that ruling, not the presence or absence of an interior total, that actually closes the problem. A SAMEKH follows Ezra.2.60 in pmarks_Ezra.json (single-witness, WLC), tier-3 weak corroboration for the rejected 2:60|2:61 sub-seam; it cannot decide the question -- Ezra.2.43-Ezra.2.57 carry no marks at all, so the local mark distribution (2.58, 2.60, 2.67, 2.69, 2.70) is too sparse in this neighbourhood to neutralise it the way the dense entry-level marks running from 2:2 through 2:40 do -- but it is the single mark in this stretch bearing on the rejected rival and belongs disclosed, not omitted. The governor's ruling, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַתִּרְשָׁ֨תָא֙ (“The governor told them” web:Ezra.2.63, oshb:Ezra.2.63), resolves the unresolved-status problem for both groups and closes the unit. It closes there because Ezra.2.64 changes formula entirely to an aggregate count, כָּל הַקָּהָ֖ל כְּאֶחָ֑ד (“The whole assembly together” web:Ezra.2.64, oshb:Ezra.2.64), with no case-by-case content left. Ezra.2.58 closes the preceding row immediately before this incipit, itself under its own single-witness SAMEKH (pmarks_Ezra.json), this row's own front seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two closer rivals were weighed and set aside. Separating the unclaimed laity (Ezra.2.59-Ezra.2.60) from the disqualified priests (Ezra.2.61-Ezra.2.63) on the strength of Ezra.2.60's own total, שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם, mirrors the logic that keeps Ezra.2.43-Ezra.2.58 one unit (no interior sub-total there); but that total closes the laity figure alone within a status question the ruling at Ezra.2.63 resolves for both groups together, so the numeral alone does not supply the disqualified priests' own resolution the way that withheld-total logic argues for merger. Reading Ezra.2.61's conjunctive וּמִבְּנֵי֙ wording as a fresh incipit of the same kind as the bare articular class-header captions elsewhere in this chapter (Ezra.2.36, Ezra.2.40, Ezra.2.41, Ezra.2.43) fails on grammar: Ezra.2.61 carries a vav plus מִן-partitive before a construct chain, a different shape from those bare determined-absolute captions, and it also lacks the וְאֵ֗לֶּה form that reopens list units elsewhere (Ezra.1.9, Ezra.2.1, Ezra.8.1, Ezra.8.13).

boundary_rationale: The unit opens with an aggregate formula sharing no wording with the preceding case-by-case notice, כָּל הַקָּהָ֖ל כְּאֶחָ֑ד (“The whole assembly together” web:Ezra.2.64, oshb:Ezra.2.64), then adds dependents with מִ֠לְּבַד עַבְדֵיהֶ֤ם וְאַמְהֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ אֵ֔לֶּה (“in addition to their male servants and their female servants” web:Ezra.2.65, oshb:Ezra.2.65), then livestock as bare noun-plus-figure lines with no construct-chain clan-or-place opener and no narrative verb, a shape distinct from the entries before it: סוּסֵיהֶ֕ם (“Their horses” web:Ezra.2.66, oshb:Ezra.2.66), פִּרְדֵיהֶ֕ם (“their mules” web:Ezra.2.66, oshb:Ezra.2.66), and גְּמַ֨לֵּיהֶ֔ם (“their camels” web:Ezra.2.67, oshb:Ezra.2.67) carry a 3mp possessive suffix on the head noun; the fourth, חֲמֹרִ֕ים (“their donkeys” web:Ezra.2.67, oshb:Ezra.2.67), does not -- the suffix marks three of the four property heads, not all four, so the feature that actually holds across all four lines is the bare head noun plus figure itself, not the suffix. Lacking a fronting conjunction is not itself distinctive -- all thirty-three entries of Ezra.2.3-Ezra.2.35 and the four bare class captions (Ezra.2.36, Ezra.2.40, Ezra.2.41, Ezra.2.43) are equally unconjoined -- but the bare-head-noun-plus-figure shape is: no clan or class entry across Ezra.2.3-Ezra.2.35 (33 entries, one per verse) or the four bare class captions (Ezra.2.36, Ezra.2.40, Ezra.2.41, Ezra.2.43) drops its construct-chain clan/place opener the way Ezra.2.66-Ezra.2.67 do, marking this stretch as one aggregate-summary block distinct in kind from the case-by-case register before it. Within that block, the shift at Ezra.2.66 from person totals (assembly, servants, singers) to property totals (horses, mules, camels, donkeys) carries no connective of its own, but it is not vocabulary-disjoint: Ezra.2.65's עַבְדֵיהֶ֤ם וְאַמְהֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ already carries the identical 3mp possessive-suffix head morphology that recurs at סוּסֵיהֶ֕ם, and Ezra.2.64 through Ezra.2.67 share one counting formula throughout (hundreds/thousands plus tens plus units); that shared morphology and formula, not any vocabulary break, are what bind the whole span into one accounting, so the interior category shift does not outrank the narrative restart at Ezra.2.68. It stays interior to one unit because כָּל הַקָּהָ֖ל כְּאֶחָ֑ד functions as a header governing the entire census report through Ezra.2.67, not merely the assembly count on its own: every line from Ezra.2.64 through Ezra.2.67 is a bare total with no narrative verb, one continuous accounting split by category alone (persons, then animals) rather than by any resumed frame. It closes because Ezra.2.68 reopens narration with a new subject and a temporal clause, וּמֵרָאשֵׁי֙ הָֽאָב֔וֹת בְּבוֹאָ֕ם (“Some of the heads of fathers' households, when they came” web:Ezra.2.68, oshb:Ezra.2.68), moving from static counts back to narrated action.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the person totals (Ezra.2.64-Ezra.2.65) from the livestock totals (Ezra.2.66-Ezra.2.67) at the category shift is the closer rival, but it fails on the same shared morphology and numeral formula that bind the whole block: כָּל הַקָּהָ֖ל כְּאֶחָ֑ד governs the entire report as one accounting sweep, not the assembly count alone, so an interior category shift carries no unit-closing force next to Ezra.2.68's narrative restart. Attaching Ezra.2.64-Ezra.2.67 to the preceding unverified-lineage notice as one long 'closing accounts' row would separately erase the formal break between case-by-case narration (Ezra.2.59-Ezra.2.63) and this aggregate count register.

boundary_rationale: A new subject and temporal clause open the unit, וּמֵרָאשֵׁי֙ הָֽאָב֔וֹת בְּבוֹאָ֕ם (“Some of the heads of fathers' households, when they came” web:Ezra.2.68, oshb:Ezra.2.68), turning from static totals to narrated arrival. Ezra.2.69 gives the freewill sums, כְּכֹחָ֗ם נָתְנוּ֮ לְאוֹצַ֣ר הַמְּלָאכָה֒ (“They gave according to their ability into the treasury of the work” web:Ezra.2.69, oshb:Ezra.2.69). The unit -- and this part -- closes on the settlement colophon וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים (“So the priests and the Levites... lived” web:Ezra.2.70, oshb:Ezra.2.70), ending וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּעָרֵיהֶֽם (“all Israel in their cities” web:Ezra.2.70, oshb:Ezra.2.70) -- a settlement formula that answers the register's own opening line, אִ֥ישׁ לְעִירֽוֹ (“everyone to his city” web:Ezra.2.1, oshb:Ezra.2.1), bracketing the whole chapter 2 register as one literary act between an opening and a closing settlement notice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading Ezra.2.68-Ezra.2.70 as an appendix folded into the Ezra.2.64 through Ezra.2.67 totals block would erase the narrative restart at Ezra.2.68 and sever the settlement colophon of Ezra.2.70 from its answering role against the register's own opening at Ezra.2.1.

boundary_rationale: A dated onset paired with a communal assembly opens the unit: וַיִּגַּע֙ הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י ... וַיֵּאָסְפ֥וּ הָעָ֛ם כְּאִ֥ישׁ אֶחָ֖ד (“When the seventh month had come ... the people gathered themselves together as one man” web:Ezra.3.1, oshb:Ezra.3.1); Ezra.3.1 itself is bracketed by merely weak, tier-3 corroboration, closing under a doubled SAMEKH+SAMEKH (single-witness) with Ezra.2.70's own SAMEKH (single-witness) just before it -- Writings marks that do not drive a boundary by themselves. Altar-building and the fear-of-the-nations motif (Ezra.3.2-Ezra.3.3) and the festal calendar -- Booths, new moons, freewill gifts (Ezra.3.4-Ezra.3.5) -- continue in a single narrative wayyiqtol chain under one compound subject: a 3ms head opens it, וַיָּקָם֩ יֵשׁ֨וּעַ בֶּן (“Then Jeshua ... stood up” web:Ezra.3.2, oshb:Ezra.3.2), and the chain turns plural at וַיִּבְנ֕וּ (“and built” web:Ezra.3.2, oshb:Ezra.3.2) later in the same verse, running plural through Ezra.3.3, which carries a number-divergent ketiv/qere at its verb (ketiv ויעל / qere וַיַּעֲל֨וּ, oshb:Ezra.3.3), and continuing nominally at Ezra.3.5 with no finite verb of its own. No fresh subject or frame is introduced at Ezra.3.4; the seventh-month timeframe set in 3:1 governs the whole stretch. The unit closes at the topic change to building logistics that opens the next row, oshb:Ezra.3.7 וַיִּ֨תְּנוּ כֶ֔סֶף לַחֹצְבִ֖ים וְלֶחָרָשִׁ֑ים (“They also gave money to the masons and to the carpenters” web:Ezra.3.7) -- a shift from sacrificial calendar to procurement, under a fresh direct object and a fresh class of recipients -- and on a proleptic notice that withholds what Ezra.3.10 eventually supplies: web:Ezra.3.6 “... the foundation of Yahweh's temple was not yet laid.”, oshb:Ezra.3.6 וְהֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א יֻסָּֽד.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at Ezra.3.4 to separate altar-building from the festal calendar fails because both halves share one wayyiqtol chain, one seventh-month timeframe, and no intervening frame-marker.

boundary_rationale: The topic changes from sacrifice to building logistics at web:Ezra.3.7 “They also gave money to the masons and to the carpenters. They also gave food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea, to Joppa, according to the grant that they had from Cyrus King of Persia.”, oshb:Ezra.3.7 opening וַיִּ֨תְּנוּ כֶ֔סֶף לַחֹצְבִ֖ים וְלֶחָרָשִׁ֑ים -- funding and materials for masons, carpenters, and Sidonian/Tyrian cedar-haulers, on the strength of Cyrus's own grant. Ezra.3.8 opens with the verse-initial waw-plus-ב-preposition-time-expression construction, וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשֵּׁנִ֗ית לְבוֹאָ֞ם ... הֵחֵ֡לּוּ (“in the second year ... began the work” web:Ezra.3.8, oshb:Ezra.3.8), a device this book uses as an era-opener elsewhere, a six-member family book-wide with mixed behavior: Ezra.1.1 (opening the book's own decree unit), Ezra.4.6, וּבְמַלְכוּת֙ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ ... כָּתְב֣וּ, and Ezra.4.7, וּבִימֵ֣י אַרְתַּחְשַׁ֗שְׂתָּא ... כָּתַ֨ב, each opening its own dossier notice and boundary-driving; Ezra.9.5, וּבְמִנְחַ֣ת הָעֶ֗רֶב קַ֚מְתִּי (“At the evening offering I rose up” web:Ezra.9.5), which opens the prayer complex rather than a unit of this narrative's kind; and Ezra.8.33, וּבַיּ֣וֹם הָרְבִיעִ֡י נִשְׁקַ֣ל (“On the fourth day...were weighed” web:Ezra.8.33), which sits unit-interior in the delivery report running from 8:31 through 8:36 and opens nothing. What differs at Ezra.3.8 is not the construction but its content: unlike Ezra.1.1, Ezra.4.6, and Ezra.4.7, which each also introduce a new royal reign, a new addressee, or a new complaint, Ezra.3.8 reports WHEN the very commissioning already begun at Ezra.3.7 formally launched, under the same personnel (Zerubbabel, Jeshua, their brothers, the returnees) and the same building project -- וַיַּעֲמִ֣ידוּ אֶת הַלְוִיִּ֗ם מִבֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָמַ֔עְלָה לְנַצֵּ֖חַ עַל מְלֶ֥אכֶת בֵּית יְהוָֽה (“appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to have the oversight of the work of Yahweh's house” web:Ezra.3.8, oshb:Ezra.3.8), Zerubbabel and Jeshua the subjects of הֵחֵ֡לּוּ and of that appointment, the Levites its marked direct object -- continuing into Ezra.3.9's closing appointment under the same office, לְנַצֵּ֛חַ עַל עֹשֵׂ֥ה הַמְּלָאכָ֖ה בְּבֵ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים (“to have the oversight of the workmen”, web:Ezra.3.9, oshb:Ezra.3.9). No new topic or scene co-occurs with the era-formula here the way one does at Ezra.1.1, Ezra.4.6, and Ezra.4.7 -- the construction's boundary-driving force in this book tracks a co-occurring discourse shift, not the bare formula alone, and that co-occurrence is genuinely absent at Ezra.3.8. pmarks_Ezra.json (single-witness, WLC) places a PE following Ezra.3.7 and a PE following Ezra.3.8, tier-3 weak corroboration bracketing the rejected 3:8-opener reading without deciding it. The move ends at Ezra.3.9 because Ezra.3.10 opens a new scene with a different verb pair (foundation actually laid, priests vested) rather than more preparation; pmarks_Ezra.json also places a SAMEKH following Ezra.3.9, single-witness, at this row's own close.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Ezra.3.8 as its own unit-opener is a real rival: its verse-initial waw-plus-ב-time-expression-plus-qatal construction belongs to a six-member family in this book (Ezra.1.1, Ezra.3.8, Ezra.4.6, Ezra.4.7, Ezra.8.33, Ezra.9.5) with mixed behavior -- three members open units (1:1, 4:6, 4:7), one opens the prayer complex (9:5), and one is unit-interior (8:33, inside the 8:31-through-8:36 delivery report) -- so the rival stands on partial family parity, not a uniform class, plus Ezra.3.8's own participant re-specification: Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the Levites are named afresh under the appointment verb, a re-introduction the bare construction-count alone does not capture. This row holds Ezra.3.7-Ezra.3.9 together because Ezra.3.8, unlike Ezra.1.1, Ezra.4.6, and Ezra.4.7, introduces no new reign, addressee, or topic -- it dates and staffs the same commissioning move Ezra.3.7 already began, under the same personnel; that content-level continuity is what outweighs the partial family parity and the participant re-specification.

boundary_rationale: oshb:Ezra.3.10 וְיִסְּד֥וּ הַבֹּנִ֖ים אֶת הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה (“When the builders laid the foundation of Yahweh's temple”, web:Ezra.3.10) directly resolves Ezra.3.6's withheld notice: its opening verb וְיִסְּד֥וּ shares a root with Ezra.3.6's closing יֻסָּֽד, and both verses carry the same underlying phrase (compare the tail of oshb:Ezra.3.6, quoted above, with this verse's own הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה) -- a direct lexical resumption, not a fresh topic. Priests, trumpets, Levitical cymbals, and antiphonal praise (Ezra.3.10-Ezra.3.11) build to the mixed weeping-and-shouting response of the elders and the crowd (Ezra.3.12), closing on a summary notice of the noise itself: oshb:Ezra.3.13 וְאֵ֣ין הָעָ֗ם מַכִּירִים֙ ק֚וֹל תְּרוּעַ֣ת הַשִּׂמְחָ֔ה לְק֖וֹל בְּכִ֣י הָעָ֑ם …, web:Ezra.3.13 “so that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people; for the people shouted with a loud shout, and the noise was heard far away.”. Ezra.4.1 then introduces an entirely new subject (“the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin”) with no continuity of scene, marking the close here rather than there.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the row through Ezra.4.3 to keep "building reactions" together fails because Ezra.4.1 introduces a wholly new cast (the adversaries) and a new narrative problem, not a continuation of the dedication scene.

boundary_rationale: A wholly new subject opens the scene: web:Ezra.4.1 “Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple to Yahweh, the God of Israel,”, oshb:Ezra.4.1 opening וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֔וּ צָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ן (“the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard”). The adversaries' request in Ezra.4.2 (framed as shared worship since Esarhaddon) is met by direct quoted refusal, לֹֽא לָ֣כֶם וָלָ֔נוּ לִבְנ֥וֹת בַּ֖יִת לֵאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ (“You have nothing to do with us”, web:Ezra.4.3) closing on an appeal to royal warrant, כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔נוּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ כּ֥וֹרֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ פָּרָֽס (“as King Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us”). This bounded dialogue scene -- with direct speech on both sides -- ends there; Ezra.4.4 switches to a periphrastic durative construction, וַיְהִי֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ מְרַפִּ֖ים יְדֵ֣י עַם יְהוּדָ֑ה ומבלהים וּֽמְבַהֲלִ֥ים אוֹתָ֖ם לִבְנֽוֹת (“the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building” web:Ezra.4.4, oshb:Ezra.4.4; the second participle carries a ketiv/qere pair, ketiv ומבלהים / qere וּֽמְבַהֲלִ֥ים), continuing at Ezra.4.5 with a further participle, וְסֹכְרִ֧ים עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹעֲצִ֖ים (“hired counselors against them” web:Ezra.4.5, oshb:Ezra.4.5) -- an ongoing, iterative campaign rather than the single bounded exchange of Ezra.4.1-Ezra.4.3, a discourse-mode shift (event-advancing wayyiqtols giving way to a wayyiqtol-plus-participle periphrasis at Ezra.4.4 and a bare participial continuation at Ezra.4.5) that marks the edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding Ezra.4.4-Ezra.4.5 into this row as "the adversaries' full campaign" loses the distinction between a single bounded exchange (quoted speech, event-advancing wayyiqtol chain) and the iterative summary report that follows in a wayyiqtol-plus-participle periphrasis (4:4) and bare participles (4:5).

boundary_rationale: The discourse mode shifts from bounded dialogue to iterative summary: web:Ezra.4.4 “Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building.” renders oshb:Ezra.4.4's participial וַיְהִי֙ עַם הָאָ֔רֶץ מְרַפִּ֖ים יְדֵ֣י עַם יְהוּדָ֑ה (“weakening”), describing an ongoing condition rather than a single event. Ezra.4.5 extends the report across a stretch of time closed by a named royal horizon: oshb:Ezra.4.5 וְסֹכְרִ֧ים עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹעֲצִ֖ים לְהָפֵ֣ר עֲצָתָ֑ם כָּל יְמֵ֗י כּ֚וֹרֶשׁ מֶ֣לֶךְ פָּרַ֔ס וְעַד מַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ פָּרָֽס (“all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia”, web:Ezra.4.5). That closing temporal envelope -- this verse's own מַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ פָּרָֽס -- reappears verbatim at the end of the later, differently-scripted verse that closes this part (argued in that row, where this row's function as the horizon it resumes is set out in full). Ezra.4.6 reopens with its own dated formula naming a different, later king (Ahasuerus) and a discrete written accusation rather than an ongoing condition, marking the edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through Ezra.4.6 as one "opposition across reigns" catalogue fails because 4:6 shifts from durative participles to a perfect-tense notice ("they wrote") introduced by its own dated formula, a formally discrete unit rather than a continuation.

boundary_rationale: This single verse is a self-contained dated notice, formally parallel to but topically distinct from its neighbors: oshb:Ezra.4.6 וּבְמַלְכוּת֙ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֔וֹשׁ בִּתְחִלַּ֖ת מַלְכוּת֑וֹ כָּתְב֣וּ שִׂטְנָ֔ה עַל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָֽם, web:Ezra.4.6 “In the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.”. Its opening dated formula, וּבְמַלְכוּת֙, names Ahasuerus -- a different king than either Ezra.4.5's closing horizon (Cyrus-to-Darius) or Ezra.4.7's Artaxerxes notice that follows -- and its own noun, שִׂטְנָ֔ה (rendered by web:Ezra.4.6 as “accusation”), is not continued or quoted anywhere else (sweep: 1/1 book-wide, skeleton tier), so the verse neither extends 4:4-5's iterative report nor supplies the letter content 4:7 anticipates. Weak corroboration: oshb:Ezra.4.6 closes under a SAMEKH (single-witness).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging with Ezra.4.7 into one "further hostile correspondence" notice loses the fact that each verse opens with its own independent dated formula naming a different king and different correspondents -- two discrete notices, not one.

boundary_rationale: A second, independently dated notice opens with a different formula and a different named king: oshb:Ezra.4.7 opening וּבִימֵ֣י אַרְתַּחְשַׁ֗שְׂתָּא כָּתַ֨ב בִּשְׁלָ֜ם מִתְרְדָ֤ת טָֽבְאֵל֙ (“In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel...wrote”, web:Ezra.4.7) -- its verb כָּתַ֨ב is singular, against Ezra.4.6's plural כָּתְב֣וּ (Ezra.4.6 itself closes under a single-witness SAMEKH, pmarks_Ezra.json), governing Bishlam as lead name beside a companions-clause carrying its own ketiv/qere pair, וּשְׁאָ֣ר כנותו כְּנָוֺתָ֔יו (‘and the rest of his companions’, oshb:Ezra.4.7) -- so the concord is contested but the correspondents named are distinct from Ezra.4.6's unnamed writers under either reading. The verse closes by announcing, in Hebrew, that the document itself was written in the other tongue: וּכְתָב֙ הַֽנִּשְׁתְּוָ֔ן כָּת֥וּב אֲרָמִ֖ית וּמְתֻרְגָּ֥ם אֲרָמִֽית (“the writing of the letter was written in Syrian and delivered in the Syrian language”, web:Ezra.4.7) -- a co-occurring topic shift (new correspondents, then a metalinguistic notice) that functions as the hinge before the actual Aramaic onset; pmarks_Ezra.json (single-witness, WLC) marks PE following Ezra.4.7, weak (tier-3) corroboration only. The verse itself stays Hebrew even while describing the coming script change, so it is kept out of the Aramaic-letter row rather than folded into it: those correspondents differ from Rehum and Shimshai, who address the king in Ezra.4.8, and that verse's own closing word כְּנֵֽמָא (“as follows”) is the actual tier-1 opener of the letter that follows, so 4:7 does not merely introduce it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching Ezra.4.7 forward as the incipit of the Rehum letter fails because 4:7 names different correspondents (Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel) than the letter actually quoted, and the letter's own address-formula sits at the end of Ezra.4.8, not in 4:7.

boundary_rationale: The Aramaic zone opens on an address-and-incipit formula naming this letter's actual authors: oshb:Ezra.4.8 רְח֣וּם בְּעֵל טְעֵ֗ם וְשִׁמְשַׁי֙ סָֽפְרָ֔א כְּתַ֛בוּ אִגְּרָ֥ה חֲדָ֖ה עַל יְרוּשְׁלֶ֑ם לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֥שְׂתְּא מַלְכָּ֖א כְּנֵֽמָא (“Rehum...and Shimshai...wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king as follows”, web:Ezra.4.8), closing on כְּנֵֽמָא (“as follows”), the tier-1 marker that opens direct quotation; Ezra.4.7, immediately prior, closes under its own single-witness PE (pmarks_Ezra.json), disclosed here as this row's front seam. The co-senders list (Ezra.4.9-Ezra.4.10) and the copy formula, oshb:Ezra.4.11 opening דְּנָה֙ פַּרְשֶׁ֣גֶן אִגַּרְתָּ֔א (“This is the copy of the letter”, web:Ezra.4.11) -- itself a tier-1 document-copy incipit -- are part of the letter's own frame and travel with it under the inset rule rather than forming separate rows, since no resumption follows 4:11 before the accusation resumes at 4:12 (a single-witness PE follows Ezra.4.11 in pmarks_Ezra.json, tier-3 corroboration only). The accusation proper turns on the לֶהֱוֵ֣א jussive, twice: oshb:Ezra.4.12 יְדִ֨יעַ֙ לֶהֱוֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֔א (“Be it known”, web:Ezra.4.12) and again at Ezra.4.13, then argues from precedent (Ezra.4.14-Ezra.4.15, 4:14 itself carrying the knowledge-root forward in שְׁלַ֖חְנָא וְהוֹדַ֥עְנָא, “we have sent and informed”, web:Ezra.4.14) to a declarative closing statement, oshb:Ezra.4.16 מְהוֹדְעִ֤ין אֲנַ֨חְנָה֙ לְמַלְכָּ֔א (“We inform the king”, web:Ezra.4.16), “We inform the king that if this city is built and the walls finished, then you will have no possession beyond the River.” -- a plural participle stating a fact, not the letter's own request, which sits at 4:15's דִּ֡י יְבַקַּר֩ (“that search may be made”, web:Ezra.4.15); the knowledge-root chain יְדִ֨יעַ֙ לֶהֱוֵ֣א (4:12, repeated 4:13) -> וְהוֹדַ֥עְנָא (4:14) -> מְהוֹדְעִ֤ין (4:16) brackets the whole letter body and warrants the close better than a petition label would; Ezra.4.16 itself closes under a single-witness PE (pmarks_Ezra.json). Ezra.4.17 shifts to the king's own voice and a reversed address direction, closing the letter here rather than folding the reply into the same row.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the copy formula (Ezra.4.11) into its own row is this rival's sharper form -- דְּנָה֙ פַּרְשֶׁ֣גֶן אִגַּרְתָּ֔א is itself a tier-1 document-copy incipit, not merely absent frame -- but it fails the inset rule's double-frame requirement: no resumption follows 4:11 before the accusation continues at 4:12, so an incipit alone cannot license a split; splitting the co-senders list (Ezra.4.9-Ezra.4.10) fails for the same reason, since neither verse carries any frame device of its own.

boundary_rationale: The addressee direction reverses and a new speaker takes over: oshb:Ezra.4.17 opening פִּתְגָמָ֞א שְׁלַ֣ח מַלְכָּ֗א (“the king sent an answer”, web:Ezra.4.17) -- itself 3rd-person narration about the king, not yet his own 1cs voice, which begins only at 4:18's קָדָמָֽי (“before me”) -- greeting Rehum and company and closing on the epistolary transition marker שְׁלָ֖ם וּכְעֶֽת (WEB delivers only the greeting “Peace.” at web:Ezra.4.17; the closing וּכְעֶֽת — gloss: 'and now' — is folded away by WEB and opens the rescript body), which hands off from address to rescript body (sweep, skeleton tier: this short spelling 1 book-wide, Ezra.4.17 only; the fuller spelling 3 book-wide -- Ezra.4.10, Ezra.4.11, Ezra.7.12), mirroring but reversing 4:8's address structure. After confirming the letter was read (Ezra.4.18), the king reports the search and its finding, oshb:Ezra.4.19 וּבַקַּ֣רוּ וְהַשְׁכַּ֔חוּ דִּ֚י קִרְיְתָ֣א דָ֔ךְ מִן יוֹמָת֙ עָֽלְמָ֔א עַל מַלְכִ֖ין מִֽתְנַשְּׂאָ֑ה (“search has been made, and it was found that this city has made insurrection against kings”, web:Ezra.4.19), continued at oshb:Ezra.4.20 וּמַלְכִ֣ין תַּקִּיפִ֗ין הֲווֹ֙ עַל יְר֣וּשְׁלֶ֔ם (“There have also been mighty kings over Jerusalem”, web:Ezra.4.20) -- the same perfect-tense precedent report naming the tribute those kings once received -- before the king moves to decree: oshb:Ezra.4.21 opening כְּעַן֙ שִׂ֣ימוּ טְּעֵ֔ם לְבַטָּלָ֖א גֻּבְרַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֑ךְ (“Make a decree now to cause these men to cease”, web:Ezra.4.21) -- its verb opens this stretch's use of the root that Ezra.4.23 and Ezra.4.24 go on to pick up -- closing on a warning, oshb:Ezra.4.22 וּזְהִירִ֥ין הֱו֛וֹ שָׁל֖וּ לְמֶעְבַּ֣ד עַל דְּנָ֑ה לְמָה֙ יִשְׂגֵּ֣א חֲבָלָ֔א לְהַנְזָקַ֖ת מַלְכִֽין, “Be careful that you not be slack doing so. Why should damage grow to the hurt of the kings?”. Only at this closing edge does the royal-voice test hold: Ezra.4.23 shifts from the king's own 1st/2nd-person command back to 3rd-person narration of the letter's reception, a discourse-level break that keeps the enforcement report out of this row.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through Ezra.4.23 to keep "decree and enforcement" together fails because 4:23 drops the king's own voice entirely for a 3rd-person compliance report -- a document-to-narrative shift, not a continuation of the rescript.

boundary_rationale: Narration resumes with the compound particle אֱדַ֗יִן מִן דִּ֞י (‘then, when...’), not the bare form: oshb:Ezra.4.23 opening אֱדַ֗יִן מִן דִּ֞י פַּרְשֶׁ֤גֶן נִשְׁתְּוָנָא֙ (“Then when the copy of...letter was read before Rehum”, web:Ezra.4.23), closing on forcible compliance by animate, plural human agents, אֲזַ֨לוּ בִבְהִיל֤וּ לִירֽוּשְׁלֶם֙ עַל יְה֣וּדָיֵ֔א וּבַטִּ֥לוּ הִמּ֖וֹ בְּאֶדְרָ֥ע וְחָֽיִל (3mp, “they went in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews, and made them to cease by force of arms”, web:Ezra.4.23) -- sharing a root with Ezra.4.21's decree-verb, quoted above; a single-witness SAMEKH follows Ezra.4.23 in pmarks_Ezra.json, weak (tier-3) corroboration only (Ezra.4.22, immediately prior, closes under its own single-witness SAMEKH, disclosed here as this row's front seam). The bare אֱדַ֜יִן/וֶאֱדַ֛יִן lexeme family (sweep: 8 tokens across 7 verses book-wide -- Ezra.4.9, Ezra.4.23, Ezra.5.4, Ezra.5.5, Ezra.5.9, Ezra.5.16 [x2], Ezra.6.13, including the waw-prefixed token at 5:5 and the prepositional mid-clause second token at 5:16) narrows to 6 bare clause-initial openers in 6 verses once those two are set aside (4.9, 4.23, 5.4, 5.9, 5.16's first token, 6.13); this narrower count is supporting material only, since 4:23's own opener is the compound form above, not the bare particle. The primary discriminator from Ezra.4.24 is subject and aspect: 4:23's verbs govern animate, plural human agents completing a punctual act, while 4:24's בְּטֵלַת֙/וַהֲוָת֙ בָּֽטְלָ֔א govern the inanimate, feminine-singular עֲבִידַ֣ת (‘the work’) in a durative state spanning years; that contrast, not the particle family alone, is why 4:23 and 4:24 are kept as separate rows rather than one closing unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging with Ezra.4.24 into one closing notice is the strongest rival -- both share a common root and report the work's cessation -- but it loses on subject and aspect: 4:23's verbs govern animate plural human agents completing a punctual act, while 4:24's verbs govern the inanimate, durative עֲבִידַ֣ת (‘the work’) that persists for years.

boundary_rationale: This verse does double duty and the seam is genuinely contested; the span itself does not move under either reading -- confidence is capped instead. On one hand oshb:Ezra.4.24 בֵּאדַ֗יִן בְּטֵלַת֙ עֲבִידַ֣ת בֵּית אֱלָהָ֔א דִּ֖י בִּירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וַהֲוָת֙ בָּֽטְלָ֔א עַ֚ד שְׁנַ֣ת תַּרְתֵּ֔ין לְמַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ פָּרָֽס (“Then work stopped...It stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia”, web:Ezra.4.24) completes the root chain begun at Ezra.4.21's decree and Ezra.4.23's enforcement (a shared root, not retyped here -- see the verb forms already quoted from Ezra.4.21 and Ezra.4.23 above), pulling it toward that row as a result-notice. On the other hand its opening particle, בֵּאדַ֗יִן, belongs to a small, 3-member book-wide set (sweep: Ezra.4.24, Ezra.5.2, Ezra.6.1) whose local discourse role differs at each occurrence -- 4:24 a resumption, 5:2 a response-onset bound to 5:1's prophetic word (argued in that row), 6:1 Darius's own response to 5:17's petition -- so the particle's function must be argued locally, not assumed uniformly fresh; here it marks a step back to an earlier point, not a fresh move forward. Decisively, its closing formula echoes the Hebrew verse that opened this row's horizon: the unprefixed four-word string מַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ פָּרָֽס (“the reign of Darius king of Persia”) is byte-identical wherever it occurs (sweep, byte tier: 2 book-wide -- Ezra.4.5, Ezra.4.24), embedded inside 4:24's own לְמַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מֶֽלֶךְ פָּרָֽס opening its temporal clause -- the same royal name surviving the intervening change of written language, with 4:24 adding “the second year of” and a prefixed preposition. That verbatim echo is a resumptive repetition: 4:6-23's dossier cites, in-book-warranted, a king who reigned after Darius -- Artaxerxes, per oshb:Ezra.6.14's own כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ וְדָרְיָ֔וֶשׁ וְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֖שְׂתְּא מֶ֥לֶךְ פָּרָֽס ordering; the Ahasuerus notice at 4:6 is a book-wide hapax (sweep: 1) with no in-book chronological marker relative to Darius, so that half of the out-of-sequence reading is extratextual, resting on chronology outside Ezra's own text. Even restricted to the Artaxerxes half, the dossier is out of Darius's sequence, so 4:24 is the narrator's step back to the point in Darius's reign where Ezra.4.5 left off, closing this whole span rather than merely finishing 4:23's sentence. Both readings have real textual support; confidence is capped accordingly.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The genuinely contested rival, named explicitly as a live seam in this book's own strategy, is reading 4:24 forward as the implicit time-frame governing 5:1's prophetic catalyst: oshb:Ezra.5.1 supplies no time-frame opener of its own -- unlike the book's other four part-openers (1:1, 3:1, 7:1, 9:1) in the book's own five-part tiling (book_strategy_draft.md §9), each of which does carry a time-frame device (1:1 and 7:1 regnal-year formulas, 3:1 a calendar-month marker, 9:1 the anaphoric וּכְכַלּ֣וֹת אֵ֗לֶּה), 5:1 is the one part-opener among the five lacking one. It is engaged, not dismissed, above -- rejected only because 4:24's own verbs, בְּטֵלַת֙/וַהֲוָת֙ בָּֽטְלָ֔א, describe a completed, durative cessation-state rather than opening the fresh action those era-openers all do. Reading 4:24 as simply the final clause of Ezra.4.23's enforcement report is the weaker rival: it shares a root and an immediate causal sequence, but it does not account for why the verse switches to the compound, resumption-marking particle argued above and reproduces Ezra.4.5's exact royal-horizon formula rather than simply continuing 4:23's narration.

boundary_rationale: The unit opens a wholly new topic inside the Aramaic zone: oshb:Ezra.5.1 «וְהִתְנַבִּ֞י חַגַּ֣י נביאה נְבִיָּ֗א וּזְכַרְיָ֤ה בַר עִדּוֹא֙ נביאיא נְבִיַּיָּ֔א…» fronts the reflexive-stem Aramaic perfect וְהִתְנַבִּ֞י (a form meaning ‘and prophesied’) with an entirely new grammatical subject — the two named prophets — sharing no vocabulary or clause-type with the opposition dossier that closes at oshb:Ezra.4.24. Two ketiv/qere pairs sit inside this very clause: the unpointed consonantal נביאה is read as נְבִיָּ֗א, and נביאיא is read as נְבִיַּיָּ֔א, matching web:Ezra.5.1 “Now the prophets, Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied to the Jews”. oshb:Ezra.5.2 opens with «בֵּאדַ֡יִן קָ֠מוּ זְרֻבָּבֶ֤ל…», whose בֵּאדַ֡יִן connector binds Zerubbabel and Jeshua's building resumption to the prophetic word as one continuous cause-and-effect beat (web:Ezra.5.2 “Then Zerubbabel…rose up and began to build”), not a separate scene. The unit closes with oshb:Ezra.5.2 «וְעִמְּה֛וֹן נביאיא נְבִיַּיָּ֥א דִֽי אֱלָהָ֖א מְסָעֲדִ֥ין לְהֽוֹן», a third ketiv/qere pair (נביאיא read as נְבִיַּיָּ֥א) that returns to the prophets named in 5:1 (web:Ezra.5.2 “with them were the prophets of God, helping them”), forming a short inclusio right before oshb:Ezra.5.3's fresh temporal frame introduces an entirely new agent.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 5:1-5:2 as a bare continuation of chapter 4's Darius-era resumption (oshb:Ezra.4.24) rather than a fresh topical unit is a real rival -- 5:2 itself echoes 4:24's own head phrase near-verbatim, בֵּ֥ית אֱלָהָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירֽוּשְׁלֶ֑ם (sweep, skeleton tier: 3 book-wide -- Ezra.4.24, Ezra.5.2, Ezra.5.16) -- but it loses on topic and participant, not lexical overlap: 5:1 opens an entirely new grammatical subject and semantic domain (the prophetic word, via named prophets absent from all of chapter 4), and 5:2's echo of 4:24's phrase reads as thematic pickup (the same house-of-God project resuming) rather than as clause continuation of 4:24's own sentence.

boundary_rationale: A new named actor, absent from 5:1-5:2 entirely, opens this unit: oshb:Ezra.5.3 בֵּהּ זִמְנָא֩ אֲתָ֨א עֲלֵיה֜וֹן (web:Ezra.5.3 “At the same time Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, came to them…and asked them”); תַּ֠תְּנַי and, two clauses later, וּשְׁתַ֥ר בּוֹזְנַ֖י enter the narrative here for the first time. Its opening בֵּהּ זִמְנָא֩ (‘at that time’) is a book-wide hapax (sweep, skeleton tier: 1 book-wide, Ezra.5.3 only) with no in-book distribution to grade as a scene-onset formula on its own, and 5:2's בֵּאדַ֡יִן is one of only 3 book-wide instances of that discourse-opener (sweep: Ezra.4.24, Ezra.5.2, Ezra.6.1) whose local role varies by occurrence rather than uniformly marking continuation or a fresh move (argued per-occurrence in this cluster's own rows); neither particle by itself carries this edge, so the front boundary rests on the participant and scene change alone. oshb:Ezra.5.4's report of the interrogation already shifts to the 1cp verb form -- אֱדַ֥יִן כְּנֵ֖מָא אֲמַ֣רְנָא לְּהֹ֑ם -- an Aramaic peal perfect אֲמַ֣רְנָא literally ‘then thus we said to them,’ even though web:Ezra.5.4 smooths this to third person (“They also asked for the names of the men”) -- the verb anticipates the letter-writers' own voice a full verse before any copy-formula introduces a letter. The unit closes on the providential deferral of oshb:Ezra.5.5 עַד טַעְמָ֖א לְדָרְיָ֣וֶשׁ יְהָ֑ךְ וֶאֱדַ֛יִן יְתִיב֥וּן נִשְׁתְּוָנָ֖א (web:Ezra.5.5 “until the matter should come to Darius, and an answer should be returned by letter concerning it”), which explicitly hands off to the document-copy formula opening oshb:Ezra.5.6.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 5:2-5:3 as one continuous move -- Zerubbabel's crew still building when Tattenai arrives -- is the front edge's real rival; it is rejected on participant and scene grounds alone (Tattenai and וּשְׁתַ֥ר בּוֹזְנַ֖י, entirely absent from 5:1-5:2, enter at 5:3), not on a particle contrast, since בֵּאדַ֡יִן's local role varies by occurrence (see the cluster's own decision 027) and בֵּהּ זִמְנָא֩ is a book-wide hapax with no distribution of its own to support a 'scene-onset formula' label. Starting the letter unit already at 5:4, where the 1cp אֲמַ֣רְנָא appears, is the back edge's strongest rival, and it loses because no copy-formula or addressee frame accompanies 5:4 -- the report still sits inside 5:3's narrated third-person encounter.

boundary_rationale: oshb:Ezra.5.6 opens with the document-copy formula פַּרְשֶׁ֣גֶן אִ֠גַּרְתָּא דִּֽי שְׁלַ֞ח תַּתְּנַ֣י -- אִ֠גַּרְתָּא (determined-state, ‘the letter’) -- identical in kind to the specimen at 4:11 (web:Ezra.5.6 “The copy of the letter that Tattenai…sent to Darius the king follows”); oshb:Ezra.5.7 closes the prescript with the salutation לְדָרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א שְׁלָמָ֥א כֹֽלָּא (web:Ezra.5.7 “To Darius the king, all peace”), its own copy-formula having opened with כְּתִ֣יב בְּגַוֵּ֔הּ (‘thus written in it’). oshb:Ezra.5.8 pivots to the report body with יְדִ֣יעַ לֶהֱוֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֗א, the standard לֶהֱוֵ֣א jussive disclosure idiom (‘let it be known’) that this sweep finds 3 times book-wide (oshb:Ezra.4.12, oshb:Ezra.4.13, oshb:Ezra.5.8); the report then folds the building observation and the recounted interrogation into one sender-and-addressee frame -- Tattenai to Darius -- that itself hosts a quoted reply: oshb:Ezra.5.11 opens וּכְנֵ֥מָא פִתְגָמָ֖א הֲתִיב֣וּנָא לְמֵמַ֑ר, ‘and thus they answered us, saying,’ after which the 1cp shifts referent to the builders themselves, אֲנַ֣חְנָא הִמּ֡וֹ עַבְדוֹהִי֩ דִֽי אֱלָ֨הּ שְׁמַיָּ֜א וְאַרְעָ֗א (web:Ezra.5.11 “We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth”) -- 5:9-5:16 stays under this one sender-and-addressee correspondence throughout, with no second incipit or address formula anywhere in the stretch, so it remains one continuous evidentiary account under Tattenai's single correspondence rather than forming a separate row. oshb:Ezra.5.17 shifts register with וּכְעַ֞ן הֵ֧ן עַל מַלְכָּ֣א טָ֗ב -- its bare skeleton כען recurs 6 times book-wide (sweep: oshb:Ezra.4.13, oshb:Ezra.4.14, oshb:Ezra.4.21, oshb:Ezra.5.16, oshb:Ezra.5.17, oshb:Ezra.6.6), though 5:16's own occurrence, inside וּמִן אֱדַ֧יִן וְעַד כְּעַ֛ן (‘from then until now’), is a temporal phrase rather than a request, and 4:14's occurrence opens a causal ground clause reporting the senders' own completed action, עַ֨ל דְּנָ֔ה שְׁלַ֖חְנָא וְהוֹדַ֥עְנָא לְמַלְכָּֽא (web:Ezra.4.14 “therefore we have sent and informed the king,”), rather than framing a request or directive itself, leaving 4 of the 6 actually framing requests or directives (4:13 jussive disclosure, 4:21 imperative, 5:17 petition, 6:6 directive); the waw-prefixed spelling quoted here, וּכְעַ֞ן, is itself unique to 5:17 (sweep: 1 book-wide) -- the letter closes וּרְע֥וּת מַלְכָּ֛א עַל דְּנָ֖ה יִשְׁלַ֥ח עֲלֶֽינָא (web:Ezra.5.17 “let the king send his pleasure to us concerning this matter”), the natural end of Tattenai's single correspondence before oshb:Ezra.6.1's own scene-onset בֵּאדַ֛יִן begins Darius's response.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the letter internally at the framed inset (oshb:Ezra.5.11's וּכְנֵ֥מָא פִתְגָמָ֖א הֲתִיב֣וּנָא לְמֵמַ֑ר introduction, quoting the builders' own 1cp through 5:16) is the stronger rival -- a genuine double-frame under the inset rule's own test -- but it loses because the whole stretch stays one sender-and-addressee correspondence (Tattenai to Darius), with no second incipit or address formula reopening between 5:11 and 5:17, rather than splitting into two independent documents. Splitting instead at the report/petition seam (oshb:Ezra.5.8's לֶהֱוֵ֣א opener versus oshb:Ezra.5.17's וּכְעַ֞ן pivot) is the weaker form of the same rival and fails for the same reason: no fresh incipit or address formula reopens the correspondence between them.

boundary_rationale: oshb:Ezra.6.1 opens «בֵּאדַ֛יִן דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א שָׂ֣ם טְעֵ֑ם…» with בֵּאדַ֛יִן, one of only 3 book-wide instances of this discourse-opener (sweep: 3 book-wide — oshb:Ezra.4.24, oshb:Ezra.5.2, oshb:Ezra.6.1), each with its own local discourse role rather than a uniform 'fresh move' (4:24 a resumption; 5:2 a response-onset bound to 5:1; here at 6:1, Darius's own response enacting Tattenai's petition that closed 5:17, itself under a single-witness SAMEKH per pmarks_Ezra.json) -- the particle marks the king acting on the referred matter, not opening an unrelated scene (web:Ezra.6.1 “Then Darius the king made a decree…was searched”). oshb:Ezra.6.2 closes the search-frame with «…וְכֵן כְּתִ֥יב בְּגַוַּ֖הּ דִּכְרוֹנָֽה» (web:Ezra.6.2 “and in it this was written for a record”); a single-witness PE follows Ezra.6.2 in pmarks_Ezra.json, tier-3 corroboration for the sub-seam this row's inset-unity argument is actively made against -- a colon-formula introducing quoted text exactly as oshb:Ezra.5.7's כְּתִ֣יב בְּגַוֵּ֔הּ introduced the letter. oshb:Ezra.6.3 then reopens with the era-formula «בִּשְׁנַ֨ת חֲדָ֜ה לְכ֣וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֗א כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּא֮ שָׂ֣ם טְעֵם֒…» (web:Ezra.6.3 “In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king made a decree”), the same device-type used at 1:1 and 4:24, marking this as quoted content authored in Cyrus's own reign, not Darius's. Ezra.6.5 itself closes under its own single-witness SAMEKH (pmarks_Ezra.json), disclosed here as this row's rear seam. The excerpt closes at oshb:Ezra.6.5 «יַהֲתִיב֗וּן וִ֠יהָךְ לְהֵיכְלָ֤א דִי בִירֽוּשְׁלֶם֙ לְאַתְרֵ֔הּ וְתַחֵ֖ת בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלָהָֽא» (web:Ezra.6.5 “be restored and brought again to the temple which is at Jerusalem, everything to its place. You shall put them in God's house”), completing the vessel clause before oshb:Ezra.6.6 opens Darius's own address to Tattenai in a distinct voice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 6:1-6:12 as one undivided royal-response arc (search, memo, and decree together, all introduced by the search-frame of 6:1-6:2) is the block's own larger-unit test, but it loses here because oshb:Ezra.6.6's כְּעַ֡ן pivots from the archived memo's mixed register -- third-person jussives at 6:3 alongside a closing second-person tail at 6:5, וְתַחֵ֖ת, naming no living recipient (web:Ezra.6.5 “You shall put them in God's house”) -- to Darius's own directly-voiced 2mp address naming Tattenai, Shethar-Bozenai, and their companions; the discriminator is addressee directness, not register absence, and it is this speaker/addressee shift the single-arc reading flattens.

boundary_rationale: oshb:Ezra.6.6 opens כְּעַ֡ן תַּ֠תְּנַי פַּחַ֨ת עֲבַֽר נַהֲרָ֜ה שְׁתַ֤ר בּוֹזְנַי֙ וּכְנָוָ֣תְה֔וֹן אֲפַרְסְכָיֵ֔א דִּ֖י בַּעֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֑ה רַחִיקִ֥ין הֲו֖וֹ מִן תַּמָּֽה, naming Tattenai, Shethar-Bozenai, and their companions by vocative and addressing them directly with a 2mp imperative-with-participle, רַחִיקִ֥ין הֲו֖וֹ (web:Ezra.6.6 “Now therefore, Tattenai, governor beyond the River…you must stay far from there”). The memo it answers, oshb:Ezra.6.3-6.5, is itself in directive mood throughout but mixed in person -- יִתְבְּנֵ֔א (6:3, ‘shall be built’), תִּתְיְהִֽב (6:4, ‘shall be given’), and 6:5 itself carrying a 3rd-person jussive followed by its own 2nd-person tail: יַהֲתִיב֗וּן וִ֠יהָךְ לְהֵיכְלָ֤א דִי בִירֽוּשְׁלֶם֙ לְאַתְרֵ֔הּ (‘let them be restored...to the temple which is at Jerusalem, everything to its place,’ 3rd-person) then וְתַחֵ֖ת בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלָהָֽא (‘and you shall put [them] in the house of God,’ 2nd-person; web:Ezra.6.5 “You shall put them in God's house”) -- so what changes at 6:6 is not the presence of command language, already mixed in 6:3-6:5, but addressee directness: none of 6:3-6:5's directives, second-person tail included, names a living recipient, while 6:6's 2mp רַחִיקִ֥ין הֲו֖וֹ is addressed by name to Tattenai, Shethar-Bozenai, and their companions as this letter's actual recipients. The decree runs through the funding mandate (oshb:Ezra.6.8's תֶּהֱוֵ֧א jussive) and the curse-sanction (oshb:Ezra.6.11-6.12), then closes with oshb:Ezra.6.12's self-identifying formula «…אֲנָ֤ה דָרְיָ֨וֶשׁ֙ שָׂ֣מֶת טְעֵ֔ם אָסְפַּ֖רְנָא יִתְעֲבִֽד» (web:Ezra.6.12 “I Darius have made a decree. Let it be done with all diligence”) — the 1cs אֲנָ֤ה דָרְיָ֨וֶשׁ֙ self-naming has no counterpart in the quoted Cyrus record, and it seals the decree immediately before oshb:Ezra.6.13's אֱ֠דַיִן opens the narrated compliance that follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 6:6-6:12 backward to 6:1-6:5 as one continuous search-to-decree unit loses because 6:12's self-naming אֲנָ֤ה דָרְיָ֨וֶשׁ֙ closing formula is answered on the far side by oshb:Ezra.6.13's own אֱ֠דַיִן -- one of 8 tokens across 7 non-בֵּאדַ֛יִן-type verses book-wide (sweep) -- marking, in its local role here, compliance narration at host-account level outside any quoted document, giving this decree its own matched open-and-close pair independent of the archive-search unit.

boundary_rationale: oshb:Ezra.6.13 resumes narration with «אֱ֠דַיִן תַּתְּנַ֞י פַּחַ֧ת עֲבַֽר נַהֲרָ֛ה שְׁתַ֥ר בּוֹזְנַ֖י וּכְנָוָתְה֑וֹן…מַלְכָּ֛א כְּנֵ֖מָא אָסְפַּ֥רְנָא עֲבַֽדוּ» — this bare/waw-prefixed אֱ֠דַיִן/וֶאֱדַ֛יִן family is 8 tokens across 7 non-בֵּאדַ֛יִן-type book-wide verses (sweep: oshb:Ezra.4.9, oshb:Ezra.4.23, oshb:Ezra.5.4, oshb:Ezra.5.5, oshb:Ezra.5.9, oshb:Ezra.5.16 [x2, the second governed by a preposition], oshb:Ezra.6.13); unlike 5:9 and 5:16's occurrences, which narrate events reported inside the quoted Tattenai letter, 6:13's opener starts compliance narration at the host-account level, outside any quoted document, paired with web:Ezra.6.13 “Then Tattenai…did accordingly with all diligence”. oshb:Ezra.6.14 names the same two prophets as oshb:Ezra.5.1 — «בִּנְבוּאַת֙ חַגַּ֣י נביאה נְבִיָּ֔א וּזְכַרְיָ֖ה בַּר עִדּ֑וֹא», containing a further ketiv/qere pair (נביאה נְבִיָּ֔א), forming an inclusio across this part with 5:1-5:2's prophetic catalyst (web:Ezra.6.14 “through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo”). The unit closes on the completion date-colophon oshb:Ezra.6.15 «עַ֛ד י֥וֹם תְּלָתָ֖ה לִירַ֣ח אֲדָ֑ר דִּי הִ֣יא שְׁנַת שֵׁ֔ת לְמַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּֽא» (web:Ezra.6.15 “This house was finished on the third day of the month Adar…the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king”); the seam into oshb:Ezra.6.16 carries no particle as strong as 6:13's אֱ֠דַיִן, so this edge is the weaker of the two and is held with reduced confidence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 6:13-6:18 into one continuous completion-and-dedication unit is the stronger rival reading on this edge specifically, since oshb:Ezra.6.16 opens with a plain vav-prefixed verb rather than a discourse particle; the split is kept because 6:16 broadens an already-Judean subject -- 6:14's own וְשָׂבֵ֤י יְהוּדָיֵא֙ בָּנַ֣יִן וּמַצְלְחִ֔ין (‘the elders of the Jews built and prospered’) is this notice's actual subject, and 6:15's subject is the building itself -- to the assembled whole community, plus a change of topic to dedication, neither present in 6:13-6.15's narrower completion notice.

boundary_rationale: oshb:Ezra.6.16 opens «וַעֲבַ֣דוּ בְנֵֽי יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל כָּהֲנַיָּ֨א וְלֵוָיֵ֜א וּשְׁאָ֣ר בְּנֵי גָלוּתָ֗א חֲנֻכַּ֛ת…» introducing a new topic, חֲנֻכַּ֛ת (dedication), absent from 6:13-6:15, and naming its own single corporate celebrant -- the children of Israel, priests, Levites, and the rest of the exile acting together as one body, matched by web:Ezra.6.16 “The children of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication…with joy”. The preceding stretch itself varies its grammatical subject across three verses -- 6:13 the named officials (Tattenai and company), 6:14 וְשָׂבֵ֤י יְהוּדָיֵא֙ בָּנַ֣יִן וּמַצְלְחִ֔ין (‘the elders of the Jews built and prospered’), 6:15 the building itself, וְשֵׁיצִיא֙ בַּיְתָ֣ה דְנָ֔ה (‘this house was finished’) -- so that variation is already subordinate to one completion event, the temple's building from royal compliance through finished structure, rather than a boundary signal in its own right; subject change therefore cannot be the seam criterion here, and the topic shift to חֲנֻכַּ֛ת carries this edge on its own, admittedly the weaker of the unit's two since 6:16 carries no discourse particle as forceful as 6:13's אֱ֠דַיִן. The offering tally of 6:17 and the priestly/Levitical installation of 6:18 continue this single celebratory notice, which closes with oshb:Ezra.6.18 «…כִּכְתָ֖ב סְפַ֥ר מֹשֶֽׁה» (web:Ezra.6.18 “as it is written in the book of Moses”) — a scriptural-authority citation formula that is also the final clause of the whole 4:8-6:18 zone, immediately before oshb:Ezra.6.19's language switch opens a new festival scene.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The same 6:13-6:18 continuous reading rejected at the prior seam loses on this edge too because 6:16 introduces a new topic, dedication, absent from 6:13-6:15's narrower completion notice, and names its own single corporate celebrant -- priests, Levites, and the rest of the exile together -- where 6:13-6:15's own subject variation (officials, elders, building) stays subordinate to that one completion event rather than marking a fresh unit.

boundary_rationale: oshb:Ezra.6.19 opens «וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ בְנֵי הַגּוֹלָ֖ה אֶת הַפָּ֑סַח…» with a wayyiqtol narrative verb form that co-occurs with three simultaneous shifts: a fresh festival topic (the Passover), a new calendar reference, and the language switch itself, matched by web:Ezra.6.19 “The children of the captivity kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month” — the switch is argued from this bundle of co-occurring discourse signals, not from the language change alone. The narrative chain continues in the same verb form through the purification, the Passover slaughter, and into oshb:Ezra.6.22 «וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֧וּ חַג…», echoing 6:19's opening verb to introduce the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The unit, and this part, closes with oshb:Ezra.6.22 «…לְחַזֵּ֣ק יְדֵיהֶ֔ם בִּמְלֶ֥אכֶת בֵּית הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל» (web:Ezra.6.22 “to strengthen their hands in the work of God, the God of Israel's house”), a summarizing theological clause that seals the seven-day festival notice as one continuous unit rather than two.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 6:19 as a mere continuation of the dedication festivities in 6:16-6.18 because both are cultic celebrations loses because 6:19 co-occurs the language switch with a fresh narrative verb chain, a newly named festival, and a new calendar date, none of which appear in 6:16-6.18's close.

boundary_rationale: The part opens on a fresh era formula, oshb:Ezra.7.1 “וְאַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה” (“Now after these things, …”, web:Ezra.7.1), the same time-frame-opener device the device matrix attests at 1:1 and 3:1. The clause immediately extraposes Ezra's name and a priestly genealogy running unbroken through oshb:Ezra.7.5 to Aaron “the chief priest” (web:Ezra.7.5), then resumes the interrupted main clause with the independent pronoun and repeated name at oshb:Ezra.7.6 “ה֤וּא עֶזְרָא֙ עָלָ֣ה מִבָּבֶ֔ל” (“this Ezra went up from Babylon”, web:Ezra.7.6) — a classic extraposition-and-resumption sentence, so the genealogy is bound grammatically to 7:6 rather than standing as an independent list. Ezra.7.6 closes the extraposition-resumption sentence itself with a summary notice of royal favor, וַיִּתֶּן ל֣וֹ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ כְּיַד יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהָיו֙ עָלָ֔יו כֹּ֖ל בַּקָּשָׁתֽוֹ (“the king granted him all his request, according to Yahweh his God's hand on him”, web:Ezra.7.6). The seam that follows is carried by 7:7's participant-widening -- from Ezra alone to the wider company named there, priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants -- together with the onset of a new narrative program at 7:7, the dated ascent report (the journey itinerary) that runs through 7:9 and is argued as its own row next; genealogy-plus-resumption and dated itinerary are two distinguishable literary types even where they abut. Against this, the wayyiqtol chain runs syntactically unbroken across the seam -- וַיִּתֶּן (7:6), וַיַּֽעֲל֣וּ (7:7), וַיָּבֹ֥א (7:8) -- with its one break at 7:9's subordinating כִּ֗י; that continuity is a genuine counter-pull, disclosed here rather than denied, but it does not by itself out-rank the participant-widening and program-onset that open a formally distinct unit at 7:7. boundary_rationale: The decree's performative opening, oshb:Ezra.7.13 “מִנִּי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒” (“I make a decree”, web:Ezra.7.13), grants permission for volunteers to “go to Jerusalem” (web:Ezra.7.13); Ezra.7.14 justifies the mission with the causal idiom oshb:Ezra.7.14 “כָּל קֳבֵ֗ל דִּי֩” (“Because you are sent by the king”, web:Ezra.7.14). Ezra.7.15 extends the same purpose construction with an infinitive parallel to 7:14's, oshb:Ezra.7.15 “וּלְהֵיבָלָ֖ה כְּסַ֣ף וּדְהַ֑ב” (“and to carry the silver and gold”, web:Ezra.7.15), and 7:16 widens the funding source to “all the province of Babylon” (web:Ezra.7.16). boundary_rationale: The pivot from funding sources to funding use is marked by oshb:Ezra.7.17 “כָּל קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָה֩ אָסְפַּ֨רְנָא” (“Therefore you shall with all diligence”, web:Ezra.7.17), the same kol-qevel idiom as 7:14 but now paired with the demonstrative denah rather than the relativizer di, shifting from a causal clause to an inferential directive; this idiom-internal pivot names no new addressee, scene, or frame, so it is the weakest tier-1-adjacent signal in this cluster and this row's front seam is accordingly its most contestable. The close returns to a vocative addressed to Ezra himself (argued in the next row).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the spending ceiling (7:21-23) from the tax exemption (7:24) as two rows loses because 7:24's announcement formula (also used at 4:16) introduces a further provision to the same treasurer addressee already established at 7:21, rather than opening a new addressee or genre.

boundary_rationale: Ezra.7.27 opens on a co-occurring four-part shift out of the rescript, anchored by the substrate change itself: the Aramaic of 7:26 (the book's second Aramaic zone, 7:12-26) gives way to Hebrew at 7:27, one of the device matrix's four tier-1 language-switch seams (4:8, 6:19, 7:12, 7:27) precisely because the switch co-occurs here with the other three shifts -- diction from official decree language to covenant-community praise, oshb:Ezra.7.27 “בָּר֥וּךְ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵ֑ינוּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן כָּזֹאת֙ בְּלֵ֣ב הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְפָאֵ֕ר אֶת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם” (“Blessed be Yahweh, the God of our fathers, who has put such a thing as this in the king's heart, to beautify Yahweh's house which is in Jerusalem;”, web:Ezra.7.27); genre from decree to doxology; and voice from the king's own “I” to a communal “our fathers”. Testing the seam the matrix's person-shift entry itself flags -- 7:27's communal אֲבוֹתֵ֑ינוּ against 7:28's own וַאֲנִ֣י -- as a candidate split rather than treating this row as an indivisible hinge: 7:28 opens not with the doxology's resumption but with its first-person application, oshb:Ezra.7.28 “וְעָלַ֣י הִטָּה חֶ֗סֶד לִפְנֵ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙” (“and has extended loving kindness to me before the king”, web:Ezra.7.28), syntactically continuing 7:27's relative clause about what the king was moved to do, before pivoting to oshb:Ezra.7.28 “וַאֲנִ֣י הִתְחַזַּ֗קְתִּי” (“I was strengthened”, web:Ezra.7.28) and closing with oshb:Ezra.7.28 “וָאֶקְבְּצָ֧ה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֛ל רָאשִׁ֖ים לַעֲל֥וֹת עִמִּֽי” (“I gathered together chief men out of Israel to go up with me”, web:Ezra.7.28). Forward attachment therefore holds at the level of discourse voice, not at the level of literary form: 8:1 opens its own list unit even while its content answers this verse's phrase, so this hinge stays a row of its own rather than merging into the list.
