boundary_rationale: Ezra.8.1 opens with the register-incipit formula, oshb:Ezra.8.1 “וְאֵ֛לֶּה רָאשֵׁ֥י אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֖ם וְהִתְיַחְשָׂ֑ם” (“Now these are the heads of their fathers' households, and this is the genealogy”, web:Ezra.8.1), the same demonstrative-plus-construct-chain opener the matrix attests at Ezra.2.1 -- 10:18 shares the register-incipit ROLE, not this formula's actual construction: its own opener is a Niphal wayyiqtol, “and there was found”, with no demonstrative at all. The demonstrative וְאֵ֛לֶּה itself is not reserved for register onsets: skeleton sweep returns 6 hits book-wide (1:9, 2:1, 2:59, 6:12, 8:1, 8:13), of which 6:12 is a substring artefact of the Aramaic word for “and the God”, leaving 5 real Hebrew tokens -- and two of the five (2:59, 8:13) head sub-groups INSIDE registers rather than registers themselves. The incipit's boundary force at 8:1 therefore rests on what is appended to the opener rather than on the demonstrative alone: the classification term oshb:Ezra.8.1 “וְהִתְיַחְשָׂ֑ם”, the 1cs anchor oshb:Ezra.8.1 “הָעֹלִ֣ים עִמִּ֗י” (“those who went up with me”, web:Ezra.8.1) echoing 7:28's closing phrase, and the regnal date. Ezra.8.2 then names three lineage heads -- Phinehas/Gershom, Ithamar/Daniel, David/Hattush, oshb:Ezra.8.2 “מִבְּנֵ֤י פִֽינְחָס֙ גֵּֽרְשֹׁ֔ם מִבְּנֵ֥י אִיתָמָ֖ר דָּנִיֵּ֑אל מִבְּנֵ֥י דָוִ֖יד חַטּֽוּשׁ” -- with no headcount clause, unlike every entry from 8:3 onward (12 of 12 verses, 8:3-8:14, carry a headcount clause; 0 of the 3 names in 8:2 do). For list discipline: pmarks_Ezra.json (single-witness, WLC) marks the front seam of this register with PE at Ezra.7.28, a verse belonging to the preceding part rather than to this row's own span, disclosed here for completeness and not counted as corroboration inside 8:1-2 itself. Turning to the marks that do fall inside this row's own span (all single-witness): a SAMEKH follows Ezra.8.1, closing the incipit line, and Ezra.8.2 carries a triple SAMEKH+SAMEKH+SAMEKH, one mark per named head-pair (Phinehas/Gershom, Ithamar/Daniel, David/Hattush); disclosed alongside the register's full per-entry pattern, since a mark (single-witness) follows every one of the 14 verses from 8:1 through 8:14, including a double SAMEKH (single-witness) at 8:3, so the triple's evidential weight is a count match inside a near-uniform per-entry marking convention, not a contrast against unmarked neighbors.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 8:2's three heads into the numbered-laity row (8:3-14) loses because those entries structurally require the headcount clause that 8:2 lacks (12/12 present in 8:3-14 against 0/3 in 8:2); the triple mark at 8:2, while it does match the verse's three named head-pairs, sits inside a register where a mark follows every entry (14/14, 8:1-8:14) and so is not itself distinguishing corroboration.

boundary_rationale: A shared entry formula governs 8:3 through 8:12: clan of origin, then either a named leader or (in two entries) a bare patronymic, then a headcount. The definite closing element, numeral plus הַזְּכָרִֽים, is attested 11 times book-wide and spans 8:4-8:14 only, absent from 8:1, 8:2, and 8:3 alike -- so it cannot itself be the criterion separating 8:2 from 8:3. What does separate them is whether the entry carries any count at all: 8:2's three patrilines (Gershom, Daniel, Hattush) are bare names with no headcount, while 8:3 already counts its own entry, oshb:Ezra.8.3 “הִתְיַחֵ֥שׂ לִזְכָרִ֖ים” (“were listed by genealogy of the males”, web:Ezra.8.3), closing on its own numeral, one hundred fifty, via the indefinite לִזְכָרִ֖ים rather than the definite form 8:4 onward uses. Ezra.8.9 illustrates the formula cleanly, oshb:Ezra.8.9 “מִבְּנֵ֣י יוֹאָ֔ב עֹבַדְיָ֖ה בֶּן יְחִיאֵ֑ל וְעִמּ֕וֹ מָאתַ֛יִם וּשְׁמֹנָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר הַזְּכָרִֽים” (“Of the sons of Joab, Obadiah… and with him two hundred eighteen males”, web:Ezra.8.9), with the recurring closing pattern also visible at Ezra.8.4, oshb:Ezra.8.4 “וְעִמּ֖וֹ מָאתַ֥יִם הַזְּכָרִֽים” (“and with him two hundred males”, web:Ezra.8.4). Two entries hold a patronymic rather than a personal name in the leader slot, oshb:Ezra.8.5 “בֶּן יַחֲזִיאֵ֑ל” and oshb:Ezra.8.10 “בֶּן יוֹסִפְיָ֑ה”, so the formula's leader slot is not itself uniform, though the clan-then-headcount frame still governs both. Ezra.8.3's own diction still leans back toward the register's incipit even though its headcount already places it among the counted entries: its verb, oshb:Ezra.8.3 “הִתְיַחֵ֥שׂ לִזְכָרִ֖ים”, shares its root with 8:1's opener, oshb:Ezra.8.1 “וְהִתְיַחְשָׂ֑ם”, a root attested 3 times book-wide -- 8:1, 8:3, and, mid-register rather than at any incipit, oshb:Ezra.2.62 “הַמִּתְיַחְשִׂ֖ים” -- so 8:3 remains a hybrid entry, not a type-specimen. The closing pair departs from the single-leader shape without abandoning the formula itself: Ezra.8.13 flags itself explicitly, oshb:Ezra.8.13 “אֲדֹנִיקָם֮ אַחֲרֹנִים֒” (“who were the last”, web:Ezra.8.13), and names three leaders under one clan closed by a single shared headcount rather than three separate clans as at 8:2 -- the two triads are inverse in shape, not an echo -- and the naming formula that introduces them, oshb:Ezra.8.13 “וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמוֹתָ֔ם” (“their names are”, web:Ezra.8.13), shares its list-incipit formula with the register's own opener at 8:1 -- the waw-prefixed demonstrative spelling specifically, not the demonstrative lexeme generally -- (5 real Hebrew tokens book-wide by a skeleton sweep restricted to that spelling: 1:9, 2:1, 2:59, 8:1, 8:13; a 6th hit at 6:12 is the Aramaic word for “God” caught as a consonantal substring). That makes 8:12|8:13 a candidate sub-register seam worth testing directly: 8:13's naming formula introduces the three names inside Adonikam's own single clan entry and closes on that SAME entry's shared headcount (“sixty males”), rather than opening a coordinate unit with its own genealogical classification and regnal anchor the way 8:1 does; an entry-internal naming list that stays inside its own headcount clause does not rise to the register-incipit class, so 8:13 stays inside this row. Ezra.8.14 closes with a single further clan before the register yields to the recruitment narrative at 8:15.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carving 8:13-14 out as its own colophon-like row on the strength of 8:13's demonstrative naming formula loses because that formula stays entry-internal, introducing three names under one clan and closing on that entry's own headcount, rather than opening a coordinate register with the genealogical apparatus 8:1 supplies; nothing at 8:13 rises to the class-header shift that separates 8:2 from 8:3.

boundary_rationale: Ezra.8.15 names a new muster point, oshb:Ezra.8.15 “וָֽאֶקְבְּצֵ֗ם אֶל הַנָּהָר֙ הַבָּ֣א אֶֽל אַהֲוָ֔א” (“I gathered them together to the river that runs to Ahava”, web:Ezra.8.15), and closes its own clause with the problem notice oshb:Ezra.8.15 “וּמִבְּנֵ֥י לֵוִ֖י לֹא מָצָ֥אתִי שָֽׁם” (“none of the sons of Levi”, web:Ezra.8.15) -- a fronted prepositional phrase plus negative particle plus first-person qatal, מָצָ֥אתִי; Biblical Hebrew negation blocks the wayyiqtol form, so this closing clause is a genuine clause-type break rather than a link in the chain. Ezra.8.16 opens a fresh wayyiqtol, oshb:Ezra.8.16 “וָאֶשְׁלְחָ֡ה” (“Then I sent”, web:Ezra.8.16), naming eleven men -- nine closed by the label רָאשִׁ֑ים (“chief men”): Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, a second Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, Meshullam; plus two more closed by מְבִינִֽים (“teachers”): Joiarib and a third Elnathan -- sent to Iddo at Casiphia (8:16-17), where the sending verb itself carries a ketiv/qere pair, oshb:Ezra.8.17 ואוצאה/וָאֲצַוֶּ֤ה, the unpointed ketiv reading as a form of the root meaning 'sent out' against the pointed qere 'commanded' that WEB does not follow (WEB's “I sent them out” follows the ketiv, web:Ezra.8.17), alongside a second pair on oshb:Ezra.8.17 הנתונים/הַנְּתִינִים֙ (“the temple servants”); 8:18-20 report the result, oshb:Ezra.8.18 “וַיָּבִ֨יאּוּ לָ֜נוּ כְּיַד אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ הַטּוֹבָ֤ה עָלֵ֨ינוּ֙” (“According to the good hand of our God on us they brought us”, web:Ezra.8.18), naming Sherebiah, Hashabiah and two hundred twenty temple servants. The problem notice and the response could be split at 8:15/8:16, but the wayyiqtol chain resumes cleanly at 8:16's sending verb and the intervening negated clause is not itself a tier-1 device -- no era-opener, no posture frame, no register incipit -- so the break does not license a row edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 8:15/8:16 into a problem row and a response row loses for lack of any tier-1 device at that juncture; a fronted negated qatal problem-notice intervenes before the wayyiqtol chain resumes at 8:16, but the intervening break is not itself of a tier-1 class, and this remains a genuinely contested seam.

boundary_rationale: Ezra.8.21 opens a new communal act at the same Ahava setting, oshb:Ezra.8.21 “וָאֶקְרָ֨א שָׁ֥ם צוֹם֙” (“Then I proclaimed a fast there”, web:Ezra.8.21), distinct from the recruitment errand just concluded. Ezra.8.22 supplies Ezra's motive clause, oshb:Ezra.8.22 “כִּ֣י בֹ֗שְׁתִּי לִשְׁא֤וֹל” (“For I was ashamed to ask”, web:Ezra.8.22), quoting what “we had spoken to the king” about divine protection; Ezra.8.23 closes with the outcome, oshb:Ezra.8.23 “וַנָּצ֛וּמָה וַנְּבַקְשָׁ֥ה מֵאֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ” (“So we fasted and begged our God”, web:Ezra.8.23), sealed by the result-clause verb oshb:Ezra.8.23 “וַיֵּעָתֵ֖ר” (“and he granted our request”, web:Ezra.8.23). The close at 8:23/8:24 does not turn on a shift from Ezra alone to the assembled “we” -- that alternation already runs twice within this row's own three verses, 8:21's וָאֶקְרָ֨א against 8:22's בֹ֗שְׁתִּי beside אָמַ֨רְנוּ -- but on the petition's own closed shape: the fast opens with a proclamation, states its motive, and seals its result with וַיֵּעָתֵ֖ר, after which 8:24 opens an unrelated administrative topic, the custody transfer, oshb:Ezra.8.24 “וָאַבְדִּ֛ילָה” (“Then I set apart”, web:Ezra.8.24). Testing the harder rival directly: nothing in the Hebrew changes place or speaker across 8:21-8:30 -- the fast is proclaimed at Ahava and the caravan is still there when it departs at 8:31, מִנְּהַ֣ר אַֽהֲוָ֗א, so 8:21-30 is readable as one continuous pre-departure block bounded by the arrival notice at 8:15 and the departure notice at 8:31. What separates the fast from the custody transfer inside that block is not location or speaker but the closed request-and-answer shape itself: 8:21-23 opens, motivates, and seals ONE petition with its own result clause, while 8:24 opens a second, formally distinct act -- appointing named custodians and weighing treasure -- with no petition, motive, or result clause of its own, only an administrative appointment. A single continuous Ahava-preparations reading has to treat a sealed petition and an unrelated custody transfer as one undifferentiated act; the closed request-and-answer shape is the finer-grained signal that still divides them.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 8:21-30 as one continuous Ahava-preparations block -- the harder rival, since nothing changes place or speaker between the fast and the custody transfer -- loses because the fast seals its own petition-and-result shape at 8:23's וַיֵּעָתֵ֖ר before 8:24 opens an unrelated administrative act with no petition, motive, or result clause of its own.

boundary_rationale: Ezra.8.24 opens a new administrative act naming the custodians, oshb:Ezra.8.24 “וָאַבְדִּ֛ילָה מִשָּׂרֵ֥י הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֑ר” (“Then I set apart twelve of the chiefs of the priests”, web:Ezra.8.24); 8:25-27 itemize the weighed silver, gold, and vessels. Ezra.8.28 turns to direct speech, oshb:Ezra.8.28 “וָאֹמְרָ֣ה אֲלֵהֶ֗ם אַתֶּ֥ם קֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ לַיהוָ֔ה” (“You are holy to Yahweh”, web:Ezra.8.28), charging the same custodians with the treasure's sanctity, and Ezra.8.30 closes the transfer, oshb:Ezra.8.30 “וְקִבְּלוּ֙ הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֔ם מִשְׁקַ֛ל” (“So the priests and the Levites received the weight”, web:Ezra.8.30). Under the inset rule the charge speech (8:28-29) has an opening frame but no interior closing frame separating it from the reception narrative, so it stays inside its host scene rather than being carved out. The designations naming the party shift across the span rather than staying constant: 8:24 calls the twelve custodians “chiefs of the priests” (web:Ezra.8.24) and names among them Sherebiah and Hashabiah, both introduced a few verses earlier as Levitical -- Sherebiah “of the sons of Mahli, the son of Levi” (web:Ezra.8.18) and Hashabiah, paired at 8:19 with Jeshaiah “of the sons of Merari” (web:Ezra.8.19) -- while 8:29's charge is addressed to “the chiefs of the priests, the Levites, and the princes of the fathers' households” (web:Ezra.8.29), a two-class collective, and 8:30's receiving party is likewise “the priests and the Levites”, not a resumption of the earlier twelve by name. Unit integrity rests instead on the row-internal transaction shape: appointment (8:24), weighing out (8:25-8:27), charge (8:28-8:29), reception (8:30) -- one custody act over one object, opened and closed within this row regardless of how its parties are named at each stage. The weighing root (compare oshb:Ezra.8.29 “תִּשְׁקְל֡וּ”) corroborates that shape only where it falls inside this row's own four verses -- 8:25, 8:26, 8:29, 8:30, not 8:24, 8:27, or 8:28 -- but the root runs six times book-wide (8:25, 8:26, 8:29, 8:30, 8:33, 8:34), two of them in the following row's own fourth-day verification (M8-Ezra-045), so the run is a cross-seam fulfilment link spanning the 8:30/8:31 join rather than an inclusio this row can claim as its own frame.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the weighing (8:24-27) from the charge-and-reception (8:28-30) at the speech's opening loses under the inset rule, since the charge lacks a double frame, and unit integrity is carried by the row's own one-custody-act transaction shape -- appointment, weighing, charge, reception -- rather than by any claim that the same twelve named officials persist throughout, since the party's own designations shift from “chiefs of the priests” to the two-class “priests and Levites” collective across the span.

boundary_rationale: Ezra.8.31 opens a dated departure notice, oshb:Ezra.8.31 “וַֽנִּסְעָ֞ה מִנְּהַ֣ר אַֽהֲוָ֗א בִּשְׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן” (“Then we departed from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month”, web:Ezra.8.31), and reports arrival with a three-day rest (8:32), echoing the same three-day encampment used for the Ahava muster at 8:15. Ezra.8.33 opens a second dated notice, oshb:Ezra.8.33 “וּבַיּ֣וֹם הָרְבִיעִ֡י נִשְׁקַ֣ל הַכֶּסֶף֩” (“On the fourth day the silver and the gold… were weighed”, web:Ezra.8.33), naming Meremoth, Eleazar, Jozabad and Noadiah as receiving officials; 8:34 confirms the count was “written at that time” (web:Ezra.8.34). The weighing root runs six times book-wide -- 8:25, 8:26, 8:29, 8:30, 8:33, 8:34, and nowhere else -- a bracket that begins at 8:25, inside the PRECEDING row, so it delimits the larger custody scene 8:24-34 as a whole rather than corroborating this row's own front seam from the inside; citing it as an inclusio closing THIS row would claim a frame that in fact cuts across the 8:30/8:31 join, so it is disclosed here as a cross-seam fulfilment link -- the charge תִּשְׁקְל֡וּ at 8:29 discharged by נִשְׁקַ֣ל at 8:33, the noun מִשְׁקַ֛ל at the 8:30 handover answered by הַמִּשְׁקָ֖ל at 8:34's written record -- not as an argument for this row's internal cohesion. The seam at 8:30/8:31 instead rests on the dated departure and the change of location alone: a new date (the twelfth of the first month) and a new place (departure from the river Ahava) open 8:31, distinct from the named-officials scene that precedes it. The close at 8:34/8:35 turns on a shift of acting subject, from named officials to the returned community as a whole.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Separating the departure notice (8:31-32) from the fourth-day verification (8:33-34) as two rows loses because both stay inside one continuous travel-and-arrival report with no new location, addressee, or genre shift between them -- the same way 7:7-10 above lets one row carry more than one date formula, since 7:8 and 7:9 each open independent date notices inside a single travel report.

boundary_rationale: Ezra.8.35 opens with a fronted, definite participial subject and a qatal predicate -- no vav-consecutive form anywhere in the verse -- oshb:Ezra.8.35 “הַ֠בָּאִים מֵֽהַשְּׁבִ֨י בְנֵֽי הַגּוֹלָ֜ה הִקְרִ֥יבוּ עֹל֣וֹת לֵאלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל פָּרִ֨ים שְׁנֵים עָשָׂ֤ר עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֵילִ֣ים תִּשְׁעִ֣ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֗ה כְּבָשִׂים֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים וְשִׁבְעָ֔ה צְפִירֵ֥י חַטָּ֖את שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֑ר הַכֹּ֖ל עוֹלָ֥ה לַיהוָֽה” (“The children of the captivity, who had come out of exile, offered burnt offerings”, web:Ezra.8.35), listing twelve bulls, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs and twelve goats; the front seam's primary signal is the shift of acting subject from the named officials of the preceding custody scene to the returned community as a whole, and the asyndetic opening corroborates that shift rather than displacing it. Ezra.8.36 continues under the same subject rather than opening a fresh one: its wayyiqtol, oshb:Ezra.8.36 “וַֽיִּתְּנ֣וּ אֶת דָּתֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לַאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנֵי֙ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּפַחֲו֖וֹת עֵ֣בֶר הַנָּהָ֑ר וְנִשְּׂא֥וּ אֶת הָעָ֖ם וְאֶת בֵּֽית הָאֱלֹהִֽים” (“They delivered the king's commissions to the king's local governors”, web:Ezra.8.36), carries an unexpressed 3mp subject that is the golah community just named at 8:35 -- ordinary consecution off a fronted-subject qatal clause rather than resumption of an antecedent chain -- and closes with the summary notice “they supported the people and God's house” (web:Ezra.8.36); both verses read as closing acts of the same arrival. Pmarks_Ezra.json marks SAMEKH at Ezra.8.36 (single-witness), weak corroboration for the close of the whole part at the chapter's edge. Pmarks_Ezra.json also discloses PE (single-witness) at Ezra.8.34 as this row's front seam, disclosed here for completeness, and a further PE (single-witness) after Ezra.8.35 -- interior to this row's own two-verse span, sitting exactly at the 8:35/8:36 junction. Tier-3 marks can neither drive nor defeat a boundary either way, so this interior mark (single-witness) is weak corroboration for the rejected split, not for this row; at that same junction the shared golah subject and the wayyiqtol's ordinary consecution off 8:35's qatal both answer it directly, rather than resting on the earlier 8:34/8:35 seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the worship notice (8:35) from the document delivery (8:36) at the interior PE (single-witness) marked between them loses at that same junction: 8:36's wayyiqtol carries the golah community of 8:35 forward as its unexpressed subject, ordinary consecution off a fronted-subject qatal rather than a fresh scene-change device, so the interior mark corroborates a split the grammar does not support.

boundary_rationale: A temporal kaf-plus-infinitive-construct opener, oshb:Ezra.9.1 “וּכְכַלּ֣וֹת אֵ֗לֶּה” (“Now when these things were done”, web:Ezra.9.1; the passive rendering is WEB's -- the Hebrew is a piel infinitive construct plus demonstrative, carrying no calendrical content of its own and no explicit grammatical subject), pivots away from the register-and-colophon material closing at 8:36 into a new narrative movement, matching in form (not content) the same kaf-plus-infinitive opener the neighboring rows carry at 9:3, oshb:Ezra.9.3 “וּכְשָׁמְעִי֙”, and 10:1. Ezra.9.1 continues with the verb of approach and its complement, oshb:Ezra.9.1 “נִגְּשׁ֨וּ אֵלַ֤י הַשָּׂרִים֙” (“the princes came near to me”, web:Ezra.9.1) -- אֵלַ֤י is the preposition אל plus first-common-singular suffix, governed by the niphal qatal verb of approach, not the object marker (Hebrew's actual object marker, את, is absent from 9:1-2 and appears instead at 9:3) -- making Ezra the addressee of the report introduced by the infinitive oshb:Ezra.9.1 “לֵאמֹ֔ר” (“saying”, web:Ezra.9.1). WEB's quotation opens at “The people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands…” and runs through 9:2's close, “…the hand of the princes and rulers has been chief in this trespass.” (web:Ezra.9.2) -- WEB's quotation marks are its own typographic formatting (tier-4) and the Hebrew supplies only the speech-onset infinitive with no closing counterpart anywhere in 9:2. The closing clause itself, oshb:Ezra.9.2 “וְיַ֧ד הַשָּׂרִ֣ים וְהַסְּגָנִ֗ים הָֽיְתָ֛ה בַּמַּ֥עַל הַזֶּ֖ה רִאשׁוֹנָֽה” (“the hand of the princes and rulers has been chief in this trespass”, web:Ezra.9.2), has the reporting princes denouncing their own class in the third person: הַשָּׂרִים֙ (WEB “princes”) both open the report at 9:1 and stand named again, alongside the rulers, among the accused at 9:2's close -- the term occurs 4 times book-wide (8:20, 9:1, 9:2, 10:8). The seam that actually closes the report is Hebrew-internal: 9:3's fronted temporal clause pivots on an anaphoric object phrase looking back over the whole report, oshb:Ezra.9.3 “וּכְשָׁמְעִי֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה” (“When I heard this thing”, web:Ezra.9.3), and the narration returns to first-common-singular with oshb:Ezra.9.3 “קָרַ֥עְתִּי” (“I tore”, web:Ezra.9.3), completing the accusation before this new beat opens in Ezra's own voice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 9:1-4 together as one “report and reaction” row blurs the sharper close at 9:2/9:3 -- marked in the Hebrew by 9:3's anaphoric object phrase and its return to first-person narration, not by WEB's quotation marks -- in favor of the weaker temporal echo at 9:4/9:5.

boundary_rationale: A fronted circumstantial clause, וּכְשָׁמְעִי֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה ('and when I heard this thing'), opens 9:3 and pivots from the princes' quoted report to Ezra's own bodily reaction, קָרַ֥עְתִּי אֶת בִּגְדִ֖י וּמְעִילִ֑י וָאֶמְרְטָ֞ה מִשְּׂעַ֤ר רֹאשִׁי֙ וּזְקָנִ֔י וָאֵשְׁבָ֖ה מְשׁוֹמֵֽם ('I tore my garment and my robe, and pulled the hair out of my head and of my beard, and sat down confounded'). 9:4 widens the scene to sympathizers, וְאֵלַ֣י יֵאָסְפ֗וּ כֹּ֤ל חָרֵד֙ ('and to me gathered everyone who trembled'), and closes on the precise time-marker עַ֖ד לְמִנְחַ֥ת הָעָֽרֶב ('until the evening offering'). That closing notice is exactly what 9:5 resumes, marking 9:4/9:5 as a scene-resumptive pivot rather than a plain continuation.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 9:5 (reading the kneeling gesture as part of the reaction) would sever the unbroken kneel-spread-speak wayyiqtol chain that runs from 9:5 into 9:6.

boundary_rationale: 9:5 opens with the resumptive notice וּבְמִנְחַ֣ת הָעֶ֗רֶב ('and at the evening offering'), picking up 9:4's closing time-marker and pairing it with the qatal קַ֚מְתִּי ('I arose') rather than a wayyiqtol continuation — a scene-resumptive seam sharper than anything inside 9:5-15. From there the posture verbs form one unbroken 1st-person wayyiqtol chain, וָֽאֶכְרְעָה֙ עַל בִּרְכַּ֔י וָאֶפְרְשָׂ֥ה כַפַּ֖י ('and I bowed on my knees and spread out my palms') continuing directly into וָאֹמְרָ֗ה ('and I said,' 9:6) with no narrative break at the verse boundary: kneeling, hand-spreading, and speaking read as one ritual act, so 9:5's posture frame groups forward with the prayer rather than back with the mourning scene of 9:3-4. The prayer body (9:6-15) stays undivided: its one interior candidate for a rival seam — the cited prophetic word introduced by אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֗יתָ בְּיַ֨ד עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ הַנְּבִיאִים֮ לֵאמֹר֒ ('which you commanded by the hand of your servants the prophets, saying,' 9:11) and running through 9:12 — sits inside the single unrenewed 9:6 speech frame rather than reopening it: the quotative לֵאמֹר sweeps 4 book-wide (Ezra.1.1, 8.22, 9.1, 9.11) and the epithet עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ הַנְּבִיאִים֮ is a singleton (1x, Ezra.9.11), with no fresh speech-act verb pairing it. It closes on the unresolved confession כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין לַעֲמ֛וֹד לְפָנֶ֖יךָ עַל זֹֽאת (WEB “for no one can stand before you because of this.”, web:Ezra.9.15) with no petition or resolution, before 10:1's 3rd-person resumption opens the next unit.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 9:6-15 alone as the prayer unit and attaching 9:5 to the 9:3-4 mourning scene ignores the unbroken wayyiqtol chain spanning 9:5-6, which binds the posture gesture to the speech-act it introduces.

boundary_rationale: 3rd-person narration resumes at 10:1 with וּכְהִתְפַּלֵּ֤ל עֶזְרָא֙ וּכְ֨הִתְוַדֹּת֔וֹ ('and while Ezra prayed and made his confession'), a person-shift seam that also recaps the content just voiced in 9:6-15 rather than merely opening a fresh scene; the crowd that נִקְבְּצוּ֩ אֵלָ֨יו מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֜ל קָהָ֣ל ('gathered to him…an assembly') is the narrative occasion that draws Shecaniah forward when he וַיַּעַן֩…וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְעֶזְרָ֔א ('answered…and said to Ezra') in 10:2 — Ezra, not the assembly, is the grammatical addressee — and his proposal runs as one quotation through 10:4's imperative close, ק֛וּם…הַדָּבָ֖ר וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ…חֲזַ֖ק וַעֲשֵֽׂה ('arise, for the matter…and we…be strong and act').
strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is 10:1-5, since Shecaniah's closing imperative ק֛וּם at 10:4 is answered immediately by the same collocation's wayyiqtol וַיָּ֣קָם עֶזְרָ֡א at 10:5 (the עֶזְרָ֡א collocation swept 3 book-wide: 10:5, 10:6, 10:10), but 10:5 turns from speech to oath-taking -- a new act, not a new participant, under the Hiphil oath verb וַיַּשְׁבַּ֣ע addressed to the priests, Levites, and all Israel already gathered, closing on its own Niphal response וַיִּשָּׁבֵֽעוּ -- so 10:1-4 still reads as the complete speech-act unit that 10:5 executes rather than continues.

boundary_rationale: 10:5 opens with וַיָּ֣קָם עֶזְרָ֡א ('and Ezra arose'), consonantally identical at the accent-stripped tier to the form heading 10:6 (וַיָּ֣קָם עֶזְרָ֗א, differing in cantillation alone — pazer vs. revia); the same collocation also opens 10:10 (M8-Ezra-053), where it launches a public address rather than continuing Ezra's own scene, so the repetition alone cannot carry the seam here. What binds 10:5-6 instead is the unbroken subject and the absence of any new participant or place until 10:7: the oath-administration, וַיַּשְׁבַּ֣ע אֶת שָׂרֵי֩ הַכֹּהֲנִ֨ים הַלְוִיִּ֜ם וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל ('and made the leaders of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear'), and the withdrawal that follows both keep Ezra as the single continuing subject with no scene-reset in between, reading as one twin-beat unit distinct from Shecaniah's speech before it. 10:6 closes with לֶ֤חֶם לֹֽא אָכַל֙ וּמַ֣יִם לֹֽא שָׁתָ֔ה כִּ֥י מִתְאַבֵּ֖ל עַל מַ֥עַל הַגּוֹלָֽה ('bread he did not eat and water he did not drink, for he was mourning over the trespass of the exiles'), which recycles 9:4's own phrase מַ֣עַל הַגּוֹלָ֑ה ('trespass of the exiles') and closes off Ezra's private response before the proclamation goes public in 10:7.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 10:5 as the close of the Shecaniah scene (grouped with 10:1-4) and 10:6 as an isolated notice would break the one unbroken Ezra-subject stretch that runs with no new participant or place introduced until 10:7.

boundary_rationale: The formal proclamation idiom וַיַּעֲבִ֨ירוּ ק֜וֹל ('and they caused a voice to pass,' i.e. proclaimed) opens 10:7, addressed בִּיהוּדָ֣ה וִירֽוּשָׁלִַ֗ם ('through Judah and Jerusalem') — a public-announcement register distinct from the private oath-and-fast scene just closed. Its content runs through the penalty clause of 10:8, יָחֳרַ֖ם כָּל רְכוּשׁ֑וֹ וְה֥וּא יִבָּדֵ֖ל מִקְּהַ֥ל הַגּוֹלָֽה ('all his possessions would be forfeited and he himself separated from the assembly of the exiles'), which completes the proclaimed terms before 10:9 shifts from proclaimed content to narrated compliance.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 10:9's compliance notice reads plausibly as one proclaim-and-fulfill unit, but 10:9's own dated, located scene-reset is substantial enough to carry its own row rather than trail as an appendix to the proclamation.

boundary_rationale: 10:9 opens a scene-reset with a full date-and-place notice: the date ה֛וּא חֹ֥דֶשׁ הַתְּשִׁיעִ֖י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים בַּחֹ֑דֶשׁ ('that is, the ninth month, on the twentieth of the month') and the place בִּרְחוֹב֙ בֵּ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים ('in the square of the house of God') frame the gathering, וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ כָל אַנְשֵֽׁי יְהוּדָה֩ וּבִנְיָמִ֨ן יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לִשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת הַיָּמִ֗ים ('and all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered…within the three days') and the double cause of trembling, מַרְעִידִ֥ים עַל הַדָּבָ֖ר וּמֵהַגְּשָׁמִֽים ('trembling because of the matter and because of the rains'). The same verb-plus-subject collocation used for Ezra at 10:5 (M8-Ezra-051) recurs at 10:10, וַיָּ֨קָם עֶזְרָ֤א הַכֹּהֵן֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ('and Ezra the priest arose and said'), now launching a summons-and-indictment speech before a newly-convened assembly rather than the sworn undertaking Ezra administers to those already present at 10:5; the charge closes with the imperative וְהִבָּֽדְלוּ֙ ('separate yourselves') at 10:11, right before the assembly's own collective reply opens 10:12.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 10:9 as its own row (a scene notice separate from the speech it sets up) is defensible on the strength of its date formula, but the trembling assembly of 10:9 is the explicit audience Ezra addresses in 10:10, so keeping them together reads the scene as one continuous unit.

boundary_rationale: The assembly's collective reply, וַיַּֽעְנ֧וּ כָֽל הַקָּהָ֛ל וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ ק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל ('and all the assembly answered and said with a loud voice'), opens 10:12 as the counterpart to Ezra's individual charge in 10:10-11. The adversative אֲבָ֞ל ('but') pivots 10:13 into a practical objection, וְאֵ֥ין כֹּ֖חַ לַעֲמ֣וֹד בַּח֑וּץ ('and there is no strength to stand outside'), which resolves into the jussive proposal יַֽעֲמְדוּ נָ֣א ('let there stand, please') at 10:14, closing on the terminative prepositional phrase עַ֖ד לַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה ('until this matter') right before 10:15's אַ֣ךְ-marked pivot to four named subjects.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the bare agreement of 10:12 from the practical amendment of 10:13-14 is possible, but both remain inside one uninterrupted collective reply with no renewed speech-frame verb between them.

boundary_rationale: The restrictive particle אַ֣ךְ ('only/but,' a book-wide singleton) opens 10:15, shifting from the assembly's collective voice to four newly named subjects: יוֹנָתָ֧ן בֶּן עֲשָׂהאֵ֛ל וְיַחְזְיָ֥ה בֶן תִּקְוָ֖ה ('Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah', עָמְד֣וּ עַל זֹ֑את), וּמְשֻׁלָּ֛ם וְשַׁבְּתַ֥י הַלֵּוִ֖י עֲזָרֻֽם ('and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them'). What עָמְד֣וּ עַל זֹ֑את reports is a contested sense in-book: the phrase עַל זֹ֑את recurs at 8:23, 9:15 and 10:2 with a causal/topical force ('concerning/because of this'), and the nearest finite form of the verb, יַֽעֲמְדוּ נָ֣א at 10:14, names being deputed to handle the matter rather than opposing it — so this notice could report dissent from the staggered-hearing plan or deputation to help carry it out, and the boundary does not need to resolve which: either way, the restrictive particle plus the pivot to four named subjects (unlike the collective assembly of 10:12-14) marks the seam. WEB construes the clause as opposition, “Only Jonathan the son of Asahel and Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah stood up against this…” (web:Ezra.10.15) — the versional reading disclosed here rather than the settled sense of the printed consonants. This single-verse notice sits between the majority's staggered-hearing proposal (10:12-14) and the resumptive golah compliance that reopens at 10:16, וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵן֮ ('and thus they did'), which concerns the golah body rather than these four named men.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this notice into the preceding assembly-response row would mute the אַ֣ךְ-marked pivot and the fact that four specific named individuals, not the assembly at large, are its grammatical subject, regardless of whether עָמְד֣וּ עַל זֹ֑את reports dissent or deputation.

boundary_rationale: 10:16 resumes with וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ כֵן֮ בְּנֵ֣י הַגּוֹלָה֒ ('and thus the children of the exile did'), picking the golah's compliance back up after the dissent-notice parenthesis of 10:15, then the niphal וַיִּבָּדְלוּ֩ עֶזְרָ֨א הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֲנָשִׁ֨ים רָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָב֛וֹת לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתָ֖ם וְכֻלָּ֣ם בְּשֵׁמ֑וֹת ('Ezra the priest, men, heads of the fathers…and all of them by names, were set apart') names the sub-group — distinct from the golah body that merely 'did so' — that then וַיֵּשְׁב֗וּ בְּי֤וֹם אֶחָד֙ לַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔י ('sat, on the 1st day of the tenth month'); this designation-verb, not the surrounding compliance/sitting verbs alone, is what makes the unit a commission rather than a plenary session. The verse closes with לְדַרְי֖וֹשׁ הַדָּבָֽר, consonantally the skeleton of the royal name Darius (matching לְדָרְיָ֣וֶשׁ/לְדָרְיָ֥וֶשׁ at 5:5, 5:7, sweep-verified, and distinct from the investigate-verb לִדְר֛וֹשׁ attested at 7:10); WEB construes the sense as 'to examine the matter' (web:Ezra.10.16), the traditional/versional reading disclosed here rather than read off the printed consonants themselves. 10:17 closes the unit with the completion date, עַ֛ד י֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן ('until the 1st day of the 1st month'), bracketing the multi-month hearing process whose outcome the register beginning at 10:18 reports.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this short bracket into either the dissent notice before it or the register after it would erase its own function as a discrete, dated process-summary standing between the two.

boundary_rationale: The register's own incipit formula, וַיִּמָּצֵא֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י הַכֹּהֲנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֹשִׁ֖יבוּ נָשִׁ֣ים נָכְרִיּ֑וֹת ('and there were found among the sons of the priests who had settled foreign wives'), opens 10:18 immediately after the investigation's dated close at 10:17, its athnach setting this class-level finding clause over the named entries that follow. The pledge that follows, וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ יָדָ֖ם לְהוֹצִ֣יא נְשֵׁיהֶ֑ם ('and they gave their hand to put away their wives') at 10:19, is a wayyiqtol with no expressed subject and so continues the named Jeshua entry of 10:18b rather than reaching forward across the verbless clan headers that follow — וּמִבְּנֵ֣י (10:20), וּמִבְּנֵ֖י (10:21), וּמִבְּנֵ֖י (10:22), all 'and of the sons of' — none of which supplies a verb for the pledge to distribute into; it is the class-level finding clause governing every entry beneath it, not a repeated or implied pledge, that holds the span together as one unit. The row closes at 10:22 before 10:23 shifts to a different cultic office-class, וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם ('and from the Levites').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting 10:18-19 (the named Jeshua-family entry plus its pledge clause) from 10:20-22 (further clan headers) would fragment a register whose class-header structure treats the priesthood as one office-class throughout.

boundary_rationale: The class-header וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם ('and from the Levites') shifts the register at 10:23 from the priestly clans just closed to the minor cultic offices, compressing three groups into two verses: Levites at 10:23, then singers and gatekeepers both inside 10:24, each introduced by the same partitive-preposition-plus-determined-absolute shape — וּמִן הַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים ('and from the singers') … וּמִן הַשֹּׁ֣עֲרִ֔ים ('and from the gatekeepers'). The discriminator is not header morphology -- 10:25's וּמִֽיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ('and from Israel') shares this same partitive-plus-absolute shape -- but header content: 10:23-24 name office-classes (Levites, singers, gatekeepers) with personal names hanging directly off each class noun and no clan tier beneath it, which marks these three as parallel minor entries rather than major divisions. The row closes before 10:25's וּמִֽיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל pivots to a fourth class-noun, Israel, that unlike the three minor offices opens its own clan-tier register rather than a bare name list, moving to the non-cultic laity as a functionally distinct and far larger social class.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Giving singers and gatekeepers their own row apiece would over-fragment a register where personal names hang directly off each office-class noun with no clan tier beneath it, the same shape 10:23's Levites carry; nothing at 10:24 opens the kind of clan-tier register that separates 10:25's Israel pivot from these three minor offices.

boundary_rationale: The laity section opens at 10:25 with the class-noun header וּמִֽיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ('and from Israel'), naming the same office/people-class tier that 10:18's priestly header, 10:23's וּמִֽן הַלְוִיִּ֑ם ('and from the Levites'), and 10:24's וּמִן הַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים and וּמִן הַשֹּׁ֣עֲרִ֔ים ('and from the singers', 'and from the gatekeepers') also open -- header morphology varies across these four (construct at 10:18, partitive-plus-absolute at 10:23-10:25) but each names an office or people-class, not a family. What distinguishes 10:25 from the other three is not its own shape but what follows it: a clan entry, מִבְּנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֡שׁ ('of the sons of Parosh'), in the construct form every clan-name header in this span takes, opening a clan tier that is simply absent from 10:23-24's three minor offices -- personal names hang directly off their class nouns with nothing between. This class tier holds constant through 10:43's final clan, מִבְּנֵ֖י נְב֑וֹ ('of the sons of Nebo'), though the clan-header shape itself alternates along the way and carries no seam weight of its own: the conjunction-plus-partitive-plus-construct spelling repeats through 10:30, then at 10:31 keeps the conjunction but drops the partitive, וּבְנֵ֖י חָרִ֑ם ('and sons of Harim'), before 10:33 restores the partitive that 10:31 dropped while itself dropping the conjunction, מִבְּנֵ֖י חָשֻׁ֑ם ('of the sons of Hashum') -- the same partitive-plus-construct shape, without the conjunction, then carries the register through מִבְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֔י ('of the sons of Bani') at 10:34 to the closing מִבְּנֵ֖י נְב֑וֹ at 10:43; none of these shifts co-occurs with a class change or any other tier-1 signal, and two clans (Harim across 10:31-32, a second Bani group across 10:34-42) span multiple verses without repeating a header at all. Every entry nonetheless belongs to the one office-class (laity) that 10:25's class header sets, rather than crossing into a functionally distinct group the way 10:23-24's cultic offices do, so the whole span reads as one register unit at the granularity its class tier — not its clan-header shape — sets.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Breaking this span at each clan-header would multiply the row count without tracking any functional class change, since every heading here names a lay family rather than a distinct office.

boundary_rationale: כָּל אֵ֕לֶּה ('all these,' a book-wide singleton -- skeleton sweep: 1 of 1) opens the register's closing colophon at 10:44 with a summative subject covering every clan just listed. Its predicate spans a ketiv/qere pair of two different clause types: the ketiv נשאי reads as a bound plural participle in apposition to כָּל אֵ֕לֶּה, leaving the clause verbless, while the qere נָשְׂא֖וּ is a finite 3cp perfect that restores finite predication to the summative כָּל אֵ֕לֶּה clause specifically -- the verse as a whole returns to finite predication either way, since its closing note supplies its own wayyiqtol, וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ, independently of the ketiv/qere choice. Either reading governs נָשִׁ֣ים נָכְרִיּ֑וֹת ('foreign wives'), and on the qere the predicate echoes the same inflected form used at 9:2, in the officials' report to Ezra, נָשְׂא֣וּ מִבְּנֹֽתֵיהֶ֗ם ('they had taken from their daughters'), closing the intermarriage-crisis unit on the verb that named it. The verse adds a qualifying note, וְיֵ֣שׁ מֵהֶ֣ם נָשִׁ֔ים וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ בָּנִֽים ('and there were among them wives by whom they had children,' per WEB's construal), before the register closes.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching 10:44 to the preceding laity list (10:25-43) as its closing line would erase its own colophon function — summarizing 'all these' as a class rather than adding one more clan-name entry.
